title.zh: 卷九十一 列傳第五十一 孝義
title.raw: 卷九十一 列傳第五十一 孝義 Volume 91 Biographies 51: Xiao Yi

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十一 孝義

translations.literal: Biography 51: Filial Piety and Righteousness
translations.idiomatic: Biography 51: Filial Piety and Righteousness

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「立人之道，曰仁與義。

translations.literal: The Yi says: "The way to establish a person is called benevolence and righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: The Yi says: "The way to establish humanity is called benevolence and righteousness."

sentences.zh: 」夫仁義者，合君親之至理，實忠孝之所資。

translations.literal: " Benevolence and righteousness unite the supreme principle of ruler and parent; they are truly the resource of loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence and righteousness embody the highest principle of serving ruler and parent; they are the very foundation of loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 雖義發因心，情非外感，然企及之旨，聖哲詒言。

translations.literal: Although righteousness arises from the heart and feeling is not from external influence, yet the aim to aspire to it—sages and worthies bequeathed it in words.
translations.idiomatic: Though righteousness springs from the heart and feeling is not imposed from without, the aim to attain it has been handed down in the words of sages.

sentences.zh: 至於風漓化薄，禮違道喪，忠不樹國，孝亦愆家，而一世之民，權利相引；

translations.literal: As for when customs are dissolute and transformation thin, ritual is lost and the Way abandoned, loyalty does not establish the state and filial piety also fails the family, while the people of an age draw one another by power and profit;
translations.idiomatic: When customs grow dissolute and moral influence runs thin, ritual is lost and the Way abandoned, loyalty no longer upholds the state and filial piety fails the family, while people of the age tug one another by power and profit;

sentences.zh: 仕以勢招，榮非行立，乏翱翔之感，棄舍生之分；

translations.literal: office is recruited by power, glory is not established by conduct, lacking the feeling of soaring free, abandoning the portion of giving up life;
translations.idiomatic: men take office because power beckons, honor is won without upright conduct, the spirit to rise above circumstance is gone, and the duty to lay down one's life is cast aside;

sentences.zh: 霜露未改，大痛已忘於心，名節不變，戎車遽為其首。

translations.literal: frost and dew have not yet changed, yet great grief is already forgotten in the heart; fame and integrity unchanged, war chariots suddenly take first place.
translations.idiomatic: before frost and dew have even changed on the grave, deep grief is already forgotten; though reputation and integrity go unchanged in name, the war chariot is suddenly put first.

sentences.zh: 斯並斬訓之理未弘，汲引之途多闕。

translations.literal: These all show that the principle of stern instruction is not enlarged, and the paths of drawing up and leading are much lacking.
translations.idiomatic: All this shows that the principle of stern moral instruction has not been widely applied, and the paths by which such conduct is drawn forth remain largely closed.

sentences.zh: 若夫情發於天，行成乎己，損軀捨命，濟主安親，雖乘理暗至，匪由勸賞，而宰世之人，曾微誘激。

translations.literal: As for those whose feeling issues from Heaven, whose conduct is completed in themselves, who harm the body and abandon life to save the lord and settle the parent—although they ride principle in obscurity and arrive, not by exhortation and reward, yet the men who govern the age have scarcely ever urged or roused them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when feeling issues from Heaven itself and conduct is perfected in one's own person—when one sacrifices body and life to save a lord or secure a parent—such deeds may follow principle in quiet obscurity, not from reward or exhortation, yet those who govern the age have scarcely ever encouraged them.

sentences.zh: 乃至事隱閭閻，無聞視聽，故可以昭被圖篆，百不一焉。

translations.literal: Moreover when affairs are hidden in lanes and alleys, unheard by sight and hearing, therefore those who can shine forth in records and annals are not one in a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Often the deed stays hidden in lanes and alleys, never reaching ears or eyes, so those who can shine forth in the historical records are fewer than one in a hundred.

sentences.zh: 今采綴湮落，以備闕文云爾。

translations.literal: Now I gather and stitch together what has sunk away and been lost, to supply missing text—thus only.
translations.idiomatic: Here I gather what has sunk into obscurity, to fill gaps in the record.

sentences.zh: 龔穎，遂寧人也。

translations.literal: Gong Ying was a man of Suining.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Ying was a native of Suining.

sentences.zh: 少好學，益州刺史毛璩辟為勸學從事。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning; the Inspector of Yi Province Mao Qi summoned him as Attendant for Encouraging Learning.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved learning; Mao Qi, Inspector of Yi Province, appointed him Attendant for Encouraging Learning.

sentences.zh: 璩為譙縱所殺，故佐吏並逃亡，穎號哭奔赴，殯送以禮。

translations.literal: Mao Qi was killed by Qiao Zong; the former subordinate officials all fled, but Ying wailed and rushed to attend, burying and sending off the coffin with full ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao Qi was killed by Qiao Zong, his former staff all fled; Ying alone wailed and rushed to the scene, conducting the funeral with full propriety.

sentences.zh: 縱後設宴延穎，不獲已而至。

translations.literal: Later Zong set a feast and invited Ying; unable to refuse, he came.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zong gave a feast and invited Ying, who came only because he could not refuse.

sentences.zh: 樂奏，穎流涕起曰：「北面事人，亡不能死，何忍聞舉樂，蹈跡逆亂乎！

translations.literal: When music was played, Ying rose weeping and said: "Serving a man as one's north-facing lord, at his death one could not die—how can I bear to hear music raised and tread the tracks of rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: When the music began, Ying rose in tears and said, "I served him as my lord, yet when he died I could not die with him—how can I bear to hear music played and follow in the footsteps of rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 」縱大將譙道福引出，將斬之。

translations.literal: " Zong's great general Qiao Daofu led him out and was about to behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's chief general Qiao Daofu had him led out to be executed.

sentences.zh: 道福母即穎姑，跣出救之，故得免。

translations.literal: Daofu's mother was Ying's paternal aunt; she ran out barefoot to save him, and so he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu's mother was Ying's aunt; she ran out barefoot to save him, and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 縱既僭號，備禮徵，又不至。

translations.literal: After Zong had usurped the title, he prepared full ritual to summon Ying, but Ying again did not come.
translations.idiomatic: After Zong had assumed a royal title, he summoned Ying with full ceremonial honors, but Ying again refused to come.

sentences.zh: 乃收穎付獄，脅以兵刃，執志彌堅，終無回改。

translations.literal: Then he seized Ying and put him in prison, threatening him with weapons; Ying held his resolve ever firmer and in the end made no change.
translations.idiomatic: Zong then had Ying imprisoned and threatened him at sword-point, but Ying's resolve only grew firmer and he never wavered.

sentences.zh: 至於蜀平，遂不屈節。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he still did not bend his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was pacified, he still would not bend his integrity.

sentences.zh: 其後刺史至，輒加辟引，歷府參軍，州別駕從事史。

translations.literal: Afterward whenever an inspector arrived he would summon Ying; Ying served as staff adjutant in the commandery and as Registrar and Attendant of the provincial administration.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward each new inspector summoned him; he served as commandery staff adjutant and as Registrar and Attendant on the provincial staff.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉二十四年，刺史陸征上表曰：「臣聞運纏明夷，則艱貞之節顯；

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia of the Founder, Inspector Lu Zheng submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that when fate is entangled in Mingyi, then the integrity of hardship and constancy is displayed;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia, Inspector Lu Zheng submitted a memorial: "I have heard that when fate is darkened by adversity, the integrity of steadfast endurance stands forth;

sentences.zh: 時屬棟橈，則獨立之操彰。

translations.literal: when the age belongs to a bent ridgepole, then the conduct of standing alone is made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: when the times are like a bent ridgepole, the conduct of standing alone is made plain;

sentences.zh: 昔之元興，皇綱弛紊，譙縱乘釁，肆虐巴、庸，害殺前益州刺史毛璩，竊據蜀土，涪、岷士庶，怵迫受職。

translations.literal: In former times at the beginning of Yuanxing the imperial net slackened and was disordered; Qiao Zong seized the opening, wantonly ravaged Ba and Yong, harmed and killed the former Inspector of Yi Mao Qi, usurped and held Shu territory; the gentry and commoners of Fu and Min, in fear and compulsion, accepted office.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuanxing era the imperial order collapsed; Qiao Zong seized the opportunity, ravaged Ba and Yong, killed the former Inspector of Yi Mao Qi, and seized Shu. The people of Fu and Min accepted office only under duress.

sentences.zh: 璩故吏襲穎，獨秉身貞白，抗志不撓，殯送舊君，哀敬盡禮，全操九載，不染偽朝。

translations.literal: Mao Qi's former clerk Gong Ying alone held his person pure and white, resisted his will without bending, encoffined and sent off his old lord with grief and reverence fulfilling ritual, preserved his integrity for nine years, and was not stained by the false court.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Qi's former clerk Gong Ying alone kept himself pure, held firm without yielding, mourned and buried his old lord with full ritual, preserved his integrity for nine years, and never stained himself with the usurper's court.

sentences.zh: 縱雖殘凶，猶重義概，遂延以旌命，劫以兵威。

translations.literal: Although Zong was cruel and fierce, he still valued righteous spirit, and so extended him with honored summons and coerced him with military might.
translations.idiomatic: Though Zong was cruel, he still valued Ying's spirit of righteousness and summoned him with honors while threatening him with arms.

sentences.zh: 穎忠誠奮發，辭色方壯，雖桎梏在身，踐危愈信其節；

translations.literal: Ying's loyalty and sincerity blazed forth; his words and bearing were square and strong; though fetters were on his person, treading danger he only trusted his integrity the more;
translations.idiomatic: Ying's loyalty blazed forth; his words rang strong. Though in fetters and facing death, he only held his integrity the firmer;

sentences.zh: 白刃臨頸，見死不更其守。

translations.literal: with white blades at his neck, facing death he did not alter his constancy.
translations.idiomatic: with a blade at his throat, he faced death without changing his resolve.

sentences.zh: 若王蠋之抗辭燕軍，同周苛之肆詈楚王，方之於穎，蔑以加焉。

translations.literal: Like Wang Shu resisting with words the Yan army, the same as Zhou Ke reviling the King of Chu at will—compared with Ying, none could be added.
translations.idiomatic: Like Wang Shu defying the Yan army with his words, like Zhou Ke reviling the King of Chu—compared with Ying, none could surpass him.

sentences.zh: 誠當今之忠壯，振古之遺烈。

translations.literal: He is truly the loyal and stalwart of today, stirring the lingering heroism of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: He is truly the loyal stalwart of our age, reviving the heroic legacy of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 而名未登於王府，爵猶齒於鄉曹，斯實邊氓遠土，所為於邑。

translations.literal: Yet his name has not been entered in the princely mansion, his rank still counted among the village clerks—this is truly what the border folk of distant soil do in their hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his name has not been entered in the imperial registers, his rank still counted among village clerks—this is what troubles the people of a remote borderland.

sentences.zh: 臣過叨恩私，宣風萬里，志存砥竭，有懷必聞，故率愚愨，舉其所知。

translations.literal: Your servant has unduly received favor in private, carries the wind of instruction ten thousand li, his will set on whetstone and exhaustion, whatever is in the breast must be heard—therefore I lead my foolish sincerity and present what I know.
translations.idiomatic: I have been favored beyond desert, charged to carry your instruction across ten thousand li; my will is to wear myself to the whetstone, and what moves my heart I must report. Therefore in my plain sincerity I present what I know.

sentences.zh: 追懼紕妄，伏增悚栗。

translations.literal: Reflecting, I fear error and presumption; prostrate, I add dread and trembling.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on this, I fear I may be in error; prostrate, I am filled with dread.

sentences.zh: 」穎遂不被朝命，終於家。

translations.literal: " Ying then was not given court appointment and ended his days at home.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was never given court appointment and died at home.

sentences.zh: 劉瑜，歷陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yu was a man of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu was a native of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 七歲喪父，事母至孝。

translations.literal: At seven he lost his father; in serving his mother he was utterly filial.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at seven and served his mother with utmost filial piety.

sentences.zh: 年五十二，又喪母，三年不進鹽酪，號泣晝夜不絕聲。

translations.literal: At age fifty-two he again lost his mother; for three years he did not take salt or dairy, wailing day and night without cease of sound.
translations.idiomatic: At fifty-two he lost his mother again; for three years he took no salt or dairy, wailing day and night without pause.

sentences.zh: 勤身運力，以營葬事。

translations.literal: He labored with body and moved strength to manage the burial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He labored with his own hands to arrange the funeral.

sentences.zh: 服除後，二十餘年布衣蔬食，言輒流涕。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, for more than twenty years he wore plain cloth and ate vegetables; whenever he spoke tears would flow.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning ended he wore plain cloth and ate simple food for more than twenty years; whenever he spoke, tears would flow.

sentences.zh: 常居墓側，未嘗暫違。

translations.literal: He constantly dwelt beside the tomb and never briefly left.
translations.idiomatic: He lived beside the tomb and never left it, even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉初，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia of the Founder, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Yuanjia era.

sentences.zh: 賈恩，會稽諸暨人也。

translations.literal: Jia En was a man of Zhuji in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Jia En was a native of Zhuji in Kuaiji commandery.

sentences.zh: 少有志行，為鄉曲所推重。

translations.literal: In youth he had resolve and conduct and was esteemed by his neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he showed resolve and integrity and was respected throughout his neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，母亡，居喪過禮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia his mother died; his mourning exceeded ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanjia his mother died; his mourning observances exceeded what ritual required.

sentences.zh: 未葬，為鄰火所逼，恩及妻桓氏號哭奔救，鄰近赴助，棺櫬得免。

translations.literal: Before burial, a neighbor's fire pressed upon them; En and his wife Lady Huan wailed and ran to rescue; neighbors rushed to help, and the coffin was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Before the burial a neighbor's fire threatened the coffin; En and his wife Lady Huan ran wailing to save it; neighbors rushed to help and the coffin was spared.

sentences.zh: 恩及桓俱見燒死。

translations.literal: En and Huan both were seen burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: En and Lady Huan both perished in the flames.

sentences.zh: 有司奏改其里為孝義里，蠲租布三世。

translations.literal: The authorities memorialized to change his hamlet to Hamlet of Filial Righteousness and to remit rent and cloth for three generations.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities memorialized to rename his hamlet Hamlet of Filial Righteousness and to remit rent and cloth levies for three generations.

sentences.zh: 追贈天水部顯親縣左尉。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Left Commandant of Xianqin County in Tianshui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the rank of Left Commandant of Xianqin County in Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 郭世道，會稽永興人也。

translations.literal: Guo Shidao was a man of Yongxing in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shidao was a native of Yongxing in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 生而失母，父更娶，世道事父及後母，孝道淳備。

translations.literal: From birth he lost his mother; his father remarried; Shidao served father and stepmother with filial piety pure and complete.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother at birth; when his father remarried, Shidao served both father and stepmother with complete filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 年十四，又喪父，居喪過禮，殆不勝喪。

translations.literal: At fourteen he again lost his father; his mourning exceeded ritual and he nearly could not bear the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he lost his father as well; his mourning exceeded ritual, and he nearly died of grief.

sentences.zh: 家貧，無產業，傭力以養繼母。

translations.literal: The family was poor, without property; he hired out his strength to support his stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor and owned nothing; he hired out his labor to support his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 婦生一男，夫妻共議曰：「勤身供養，力猶不足，若養此兒，則所費者大。

translations.literal: His wife bore a son; husband and wife together discussed and said: "Laboring the body to provide support, strength is still insufficient; if we raise this child, the expense will be great."
translations.idiomatic: When his wife bore a son, they agreed: "We barely have strength enough to support our elders; raising this child would cost too much."

sentences.zh: 」乃垂泣瘞之。

translations.literal: " Then weeping they buried him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, they buried the infant alive.

sentences.zh: 母亡，負土成墳，親戚咸共賻助，微有所受。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he carried earth to make the mound; relatives all together contributed funeral gifts, and he accepted only a little.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, he carried earth to build the mound himself; relatives offered funeral gifts, but he accepted only a little.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，傭賃倍還先直。

translations.literal: When burial was finished, he doubled the hire payment and returned the prior advance.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he paid double the wages he owed and returned every advance he had taken.

sentences.zh: 服除後，哀戚思慕，終身如喪者，以為追遠之思，無時去心，故未嘗釋衣｛巾臽｝。

translations.literal: After mourning ended, grief and longing for the distant—his whole life like one in mourning; thinking that the thought of honoring the distant never left the heart, therefore he never removed his simple mourning garment.
translations.idiomatic: After formal mourning ended, his grief and longing never ceased; honoring the dead never left his heart, and he never laid aside his simple mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 仁厚之風，行於鄉黨，鄰村小大，莫有呼其名者。

translations.literal: The wind of benevolence and depth walked in the village lanes; in neighboring hamlets young and old, none called him by his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: His benevolence was known throughout the village; in neighboring hamlets young and old alike never called him by his personal name.

sentences.zh: 嘗與人共於山陰市貨物，誤得一千錢，當時不覺，分背方悟。

translations.literal: Once he traded goods with another in Shanyin market and by mistake received a thousand cash; at the time he did not notice; when they parted ways he realized.
translations.idiomatic: Once while selling goods with a partner in Shanyin market he took a thousand cash too many by mistake and did not notice until they had parted.

sentences.zh: 請其伴求以此錢追還本主，伴大笑不答。

translations.literal: He asked his companion to seek with this money and return it to the original owner; the companion laughed greatly and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: He asked his companion to help return the money to its owner; the companion only laughed and refused.

sentences.zh: 世道以己錢充數送還之，錢主驚歎，以半直與世道，世道委之而去。

translations.literal: Shidao used his own money to make up the sum and sent it back; the owner of the money was startled and sighed, giving half the value to Shidao; Shidao cast it aside and left.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao made up the sum from his own purse and returned it; the owner, astonished, offered him half as a reward, but Shidao left it and walked away.

sentences.zh: 元嘉四年，遣大使巡行天下，散騎常侍袁愉表其淳行，太祖嘉之，敕郡榜表閭門，蠲其稅調，改所居獨楓里為孝行焉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanjia an envoy was sent to tour the realm; Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Yu memorialized his pure conduct; the Founder praised it, ordered the commandery to post a placard at the lane gate, remitted his taxes and levies, and changed his residence's Lone Maple Hamlet to Hamlet of Filial Conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanjia a touring envoy reported his conduct; Yuan Yu, Attendant-in-Ordinary, memorialized his integrity; the emperor commended him, ordered a placard posted at his gate, remitted his taxes, and renamed Lone Maple Hamlet Hamlet of Filial Conduct.

sentences.zh: 太守孟顗察孝廉，不就。

translations.literal: The Grand Administrator Meng Yi nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator Meng Yi nominated him as Filial and Incorrupt, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 子原平，字長泰，又稟至行，養親必己力。

translations.literal: His son Yuan Ping, style Changtai, again received ultimate conduct; in supporting parents he must use his own strength.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan Ping, styled Changtai, inherited the same supreme conduct and always supported his parents by his own labor alone.

sentences.zh: 性閑木功，傭賃以給供養。

translations.literal: By nature skilled in woodwork, he hired out labor to supply support.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled by nature at carpentry, he hired out his labor to provide for his parents.

sentences.zh: 性謙虛，每為人作匠，取散夫價。

translations.literal: By nature modest, whenever he worked as a craftsman for others he took only the wage of a day laborer.
translations.idiomatic: Modest by nature, whenever he worked as a craftsman for others he charged only a day laborer's wage.

sentences.zh: 主人設食，原平自以家貧，父母不辦有肴味，唯飧鹽飯而已。

translations.literal: When the master set out food, Ping considered that his family was poor and his parents could not provide delicacies, and he ate only salted rice.
translations.idiomatic: When employers offered him a meal, he would eat only plain salted rice, thinking that at home his parents could afford no delicacies.

sentences.zh: 若家或無食，則虛中竟日，義不獨飽；

translations.literal: if at home there was sometimes no food, then he would go empty in the belly all day—by righteousness he would not eat his fill alone;
translations.idiomatic: If the household sometimes had no food, he would go hungry all day rather than eat his fill while his parents went without;

sentences.zh: 要須日暮作畢，受直歸家，於里中買糴，然後舉爨。

translations.literal: he had to wait until work was finished at dusk, receive payment and return home, buy grain in the hamlet, and only then kindle the stove.
translations.idiomatic: he waited until dusk when the day's work was done, took his wages home, bought grain in the village, and only then cooked the family meal.

sentences.zh: 父抱篤疾彌年，原平衣不解帶，口不嘗鹽菜者，跨積寒暑；

translations.literal: His father bore grave illness for a full year; Ping did not undo his belt or garments, and did not taste salted vegetables—spanning accumulated cold and heat;
translations.idiomatic: When his father lay gravely ill for a year, Ping never unfastened his belt or tasted seasoned food, through winter and summer alike;

sentences.zh: 又未嘗睡臥。

translations.literal: nor did he ever lie down to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: nor did he ever lie down to sleep.

sentences.zh: 父亡，哭踴慟絕，數日方蘇。

translations.literal: When his father died, he wept and stamped in grief until he collapsed; several days passed before he revived.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he wept and stamped until he collapsed; several days passed before he revived.

sentences.zh: 以為奉終之義，情禮所畢，營壙凶功，不欲假人。

translations.literal: He considered that in the duty of serving the end, feeling and ritual were fulfilled; in arranging the tomb and funeral works he did not wish to borrow others.
translations.idiomatic: He held that the duty of laying a parent to rest must be fulfilled in person and would not entrust the burial to others.

sentences.zh: 本雖智巧，而不解作墓，乃訪邑中有營墓者，助人運力，經時展勤，久乃閑練。

translations.literal: Although by nature clever, he did not understand building tombs; he then sought in the district those who built tombs, helped others move strength, and over time extended diligence until after long he became skilled.
translations.idiomatic: Though clever by nature, he did not know how to build a tomb; he found those in the district who did and helped them until, after long practice, he became skilled.

sentences.zh: 又自賣十夫，以供眾費。

translations.literal: He also sold himself for ten days' labor to supply the collective expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He also sold himself into ten days' labor to pay the funeral costs.

sentences.zh: 窀穸之事，儉而當禮，性無術學，因心自然。

translations.literal: Matters of burial were frugal yet fitting ritual; by nature he had no technical learning—it came from the heart naturally.
translations.idiomatic: The burial was frugal yet proper; he had no formal training, only what his heart prompted.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，詣所買主，執役無懈，與諸奴分務。

translations.literal: When burial was finished, he went to the master who had bought his labor and performed service without slack, sharing tasks with the other bondservants.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he went to the man who had bought his labor and worked without slack alongside the other servants.

sentences.zh: 每讓逸取勞，主人不忍使，每遣之，原平服勤，未曾暫替。

translations.literal: Each time he yielded ease and took labor; the master could not bear to use him and each time sent him away, but Ping served diligently and never briefly substituted rest.
translations.idiomatic: He always chose the harder tasks; his master, pitying him, tried to send him away, but Ping worked diligently and never took a break.

sentences.zh: 所餘私夫，傭賃養母，有餘聚以自贖。

translations.literal: The remaining private days of labor he hired out to support his mother; what was left he gathered to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: With the days of labor that remained his own, he hired out work to support his mother and saved what he could to buy back his freedom.

sentences.zh: 本性智巧，既學構塚，尤善其事，每至吉歲，求者盈門。

translations.literal: By nature clever, once he had learned tomb-building he was especially good at it; each year when days were auspicious, seekers filled the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Clever by nature, once he had learned tomb-building he excelled at it; in auspicious years clients filled his gate.

sentences.zh: 原平所赴，必自貧始，既取賤價，又以夫日助之。

translations.literal: Those Ping attended to, he must begin with the poor; he both took a low price and also used his labor days to help them.
translations.idiomatic: He always took the poorest clients first, charged the lowest price, and often added extra days of labor at no charge.

sentences.zh: 父喪既終，自起兩間小屋，以為祠堂。

translations.literal: When his father's mourning was finished, he himself raised two small rooms as an ancestral hall.
translations.idiomatic: When his father's mourning ended, he built two small rooms himself to serve as a shrine.

sentences.zh: 每至節歲烝嘗，於此數日中，哀思，絕飲粥。

translations.literal: Whenever the seasonal offerings of the year came, on those several days he was sunk in grief and cut off gruel and drink.
translations.idiomatic: At each seasonal offering he spent those days in grief and took no food or drink.

sentences.zh: 父服除後，不復食魚肉。

translations.literal: After his father's mourning ended, he never again ate fish or meat.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's mourning ended, he never again ate fish or meat.

sentences.zh: 於母前，示有所啖，在私室，未曾妄嘗。

translations.literal: Before his mother he showed that he had something to eat; in private rooms he never tasted it rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Before his mother he pretended to eat, but in private he never touched meat.

sentences.zh: 自此迄終，三十餘載。

translations.literal: From this until the end, more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He kept this up for more than thirty years, until his death.

sentences.zh: 高陽許瑤之居在永興，罷建安郡丞還家，以綿一斤遺原平。

translations.literal: Xu Yaozhi of Gaoyang dwelt in Yongxing; dismissed as Assistant Administrator of Jian'an Commandery he returned home and gave Ping one jin of cotton.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yaozhi of Gaoyang, living in Yongxing, had retired as Assistant Administrator of Jian'an and sent Ping a pound of cotton.

sentences.zh: 原平不受，送而復反者前後數十。

translations.literal: Ping would not accept; sending and returning back and forth came to several tens in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Ping refused it; the gift was sent back and forth dozens of times.

sentences.zh: 瑤之乃自往曰：「今歲過寒，而建安綿好，以此奉尊上下耳。

translations.literal: Yaozhi then went in person and said: "This year is excessively cold, and Jian'an cotton is good—therefore I offer this to honor your elders, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Yaozhi came in person and said, "This winter is bitterly cold, and Jian'an cotton is excellent—I offer this only for your parents' sake."

sentences.zh: 」原平乃拜而受之。

translations.literal: " Ping then bowed and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Ping bow and accept it.

sentences.zh: 及母終，毀瘠彌甚，僅乃免喪。

translations.literal: When his mother ended her life, his emaciation from grief was ever more severe; he barely survived mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, his grief left him so wasted that he barely survived the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 墓前有數十畝田，不屬原平，每至農月，耕者恆裸袒，原平不欲使人慢其墳墓，乃販質家資，貴買此田。

translations.literal: Before the tomb were several tens of mu of fields not belonging to Ping; each farming month the plowmen were always bare to the waist; Ping did not wish to let people slight his tomb mound, and so pawned and sold family property to buy this land at a high price.
translations.idiomatic: Several tens of mu before the tomb did not belong to him; each planting season the farmers worked stripped to the waist. Unwilling to let anyone treat his parents' grave with disrespect, he pawned his belongings and bought the land at a high price.

sentences.zh: 三農之月，輒束帶垂泣，躬自耕墾。

translations.literal: In the three farming months he would gird his belt and weep, personally plowing and opening the soil.
translations.idiomatic: In the farming months he would gird himself and weep as he plowed the land himself.

sentences.zh: 每出市賣物，人問幾錢，裁言其半，如此積時，邑人皆共識悉，輒加本價與之。

translations.literal: Whenever he went to market to sell goods, if people asked how much, he would speak only half; after such accumulation of time the townspeople all knew him familiarly and would add the full price for him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he sold goods in market and was asked the price, he named only half. In time the townspeople all knew him and paid the full price anyway.

sentences.zh: 彼此相讓，欲買者稍稍減價，要使微賤，然後取直。

translations.literal: Each side yielding to the other, buyers would little by little reduce the price, wanting to make it slightly cheap, and only then would he take payment.
translations.idiomatic: Buyer and seller would bargain down the price until it was very low, and only then would he accept payment.

sentences.zh: 居宅下濕，繞宅為溝，以通淤水。

translations.literal: His dwelling was low and damp; he dug ditches around the dwelling to drain stagnant water.
translations.idiomatic: His house stood on damp ground; he dug ditches around it to drain the water.

sentences.zh: 宅上種少竹，春月夜有盜其筍者，原平偶起見之，盜者奔走墜溝。

translations.literal: Above the dwelling he planted a little bamboo; on a spring night in moonlight someone stole his shoots; Ping happened to rise and see it; the thief ran and fell into the ditch.
translations.idiomatic: He planted a few bamboo shoots by the house; one spring night a thief came for the young shoots. Ping happened to wake and see him; the thief fled and fell into the ditch.

sentences.zh: 原平自以不能廣施，至使此人顛沛，乃於所植竹處溝上立小橋，令足通行，又采筍置籬外。

translations.literal: Ping considered that he could not broadly give, yet had brought this person to hardship; therefore over the ditch where the bamboo was planted he set a small bridge so feet could pass, and also gathered shoots and placed them outside the fence.
translations.idiomatic: Ping blamed himself for not being generous enough to spare the thief such distress; he built a small bridge over the ditch by the bamboo and left shoots outside the fence for anyone to take.

sentences.zh: 鄰曲慚愧，無復取者。

translations.literal: Neighbors were ashamed, and there were none who took again.
translations.idiomatic: The neighbors were ashamed, and no one stole his bamboo again.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，原平號哭致慟，日食麥料一枚，如此五日。

translations.literal: The Founder Emperor collapsed; Yuan Ping wailed and reached deepest grief, each day eating one pellet of barley gruel, thus for five days.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen died, Yuan Ping wailed in deepest grief, eating only one pellet of barley gruel a day for five days.

sentences.zh: 人或問之曰：「誰非王民，何獨如此？

translations.literal: Someone asked him, saying: "Who is not the king's subject—why alone thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked him, "We are all subjects of the throne—why grieve so much more than others?"

sentences.zh: 」原平泣而答曰：「吾家見異先朝，蒙褒贊之賞，不能報恩，私心感慟耳。

translations.literal: Yuan Ping wept and replied: "My family received special favor from the previous court and was granted commendation and reward; I cannot repay that grace—it is private feeling moved to grief, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ping wept and answered, "My family received extraordinary favor from the previous reign and was honored with praise and reward. I have been unable to repay that debt, and the grief in my heart is overwhelming."

sentences.zh: 」又以種爪為業。

translations.literal: He also took growing melons as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He also made his living growing melons.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明七年大旱，瓜瀆不復通船，縣官劉僧秀愍其窮老，下瀆水與之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daming under Emperor Shizu there was great drought; the Gua Sluice no longer passed boats. The county official Liu Sengxiu pitied his poverty and old age and released sluice water for him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Daming era, a severe drought left the Gua Sluice too shallow for boats. County official Liu Sengxiu, pitying Yuan Ping's poverty and age, released water from the sluice for his benefit.

sentences.zh: 原平曰：「普天大旱，百姓俱困，豈可減溉田之水，以通運瓜之船。

translations.literal: Yuan Ping said: "Under all heaven there is drought; the common people all suffer—how can one reduce water for irrigating fields in order to pass boats transporting melons?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ping said, "All the land is in drought and the people are suffering everywhere. How can I divert irrigation water just to float boats carrying my melons?"

sentences.zh: 」乃步從他道往錢唐貨賣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he walked by another route to Qiantang to sell his goods.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he walked by another route to Qiantang to sell his melons.

sentences.zh: 每行來，見人牽埭未過，輒迅楫助之；

translations.literal: Whenever he traveled, if he saw people towing at a dam and not yet across, he would swiftly row to help them;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he traveled and saw people struggling to haul boats over a dam, he would quickly take up an oar to help;

sentences.zh: 己自引船，不假旁力。

translations.literal: when towing his own boat, he did not borrow others' strength.
translations.idiomatic: when it was his own boat, he pulled it himself and never asked others for help.

sentences.zh: 若自船已渡，後人未及，常停住須待，以此為常。

translations.literal: If his own boat had already crossed but those behind had not yet arrived, he would always stop and wait—this was his constant habit.
translations.idiomatic: If his boat had already crossed but others behind had not, he always stopped and waited for them. That was his custom.

sentences.zh: 嘗於縣南郭鳳埭助人引船，遇有相鬥者，為吏所錄，聞者逃散，唯原平獨住。

translations.literal: Once at Feng Dam south of the county wall he was helping tow boats when people fighting were recorded by clerks; those who heard fled, and only Yuan Ping remained alone.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while helping tow boats at Feng Dam south of the county seat, he came upon a fight. The clerks seized everyone involved; the others fled, but Yuan Ping alone stayed.

sentences.zh: 吏執以送縣，縣令新到，未相諳悉，將加嚴罰。

translations.literal: The clerk seized and sent him to the county; the magistrate had newly arrived and was not yet mutually familiar with him, and was about to impose severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk seized him and sent him to the county office. The magistrate had just arrived and did not know him, and was about to punish him severely.

sentences.zh: 原平解衣就罪，義無一言。

translations.literal: Yuan Ping removed his clothes to accept punishment; in righteousness he did not speak a word.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ping stripped to accept punishment and said not a word in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 左右小大咸稽顙請救，然後得免。

translations.literal: Those small and great all around kowtowed pleading for his rescue, and only then was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone around him, high and low, kowtowed and pleaded for him, and only then was he released.

sentences.zh: 由來不謁官長，自此以後，乃脩民敬。

translations.literal: From the beginning he had never visited official superiors; from this time afterward, he then cultivated civility toward the people.
translations.idiomatic: He had never before called on his superiors, but from that time on he began paying the respects due to local officials.

sentences.zh: 太守王僧郎察教廉，不就。

translations.literal: Prefect Wang Shilang inspected and recommended him for integrity; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Wang Shilang inspected his conduct and recommended him as incorrupt, but he declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 太守蔡興宗臨郡，深加貴異，以私米饋原平及山陰朱百年妻，教曰：「秩年之貺，著自國書，餼貧之典，有聞甲令。

translations.literal: Prefect Cai Xingzong came to the commandery and deeply honored him, sending private rice as a gift to Yuan Ping and to Zhu Bainian's wife of Shanyin, with instructions saying: "Rank-year gifts are recorded in national documents; the ritual of providing for the poor is known in top decrees."
translations.idiomatic: When Prefect Cai Xingzong arrived in the commandery, he held Yuan Ping in high esteem and sent him private gifts of rice, as well as rice for Zhu Bainian's widow in Shanyin. His instruction read, "Gifts tied to rank and age are set down in the national statutes, and the practice of relieving the poor is established in the highest decrees."

sentences.zh: 況高柴窮老，萊婦屯暮者哉。

translations.literal: How much more Gaochai in poverty and old age, and the widow of Lai in her twilight years!
translations.idiomatic: How much more, then, for men like Gaochai in poverty and old age, or the widow of Lai in her declining years!

sentences.zh: 永興郭原平世稟孝德，洞業儲靈，深仁絕操，追風曠古，棲貞處約，華耇方嚴。

translations.literal: Yongxing's Guo Yuanping through generations inherited filial virtue, profound attainment stored with spirit, deep benevolence surpassing ordinary conduct, chasing the wind across antiquity, dwelling in integrity in frugality, splendid old age square and stern.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuanping of Yongxing comes from generations of filial virtue, with inner depth and stored grace, profound benevolence and extraordinary integrity, a character that reaches back through the ages, dwelling in integrity and frugality even in honored old age.

sentences.zh: 山陰朱百年道終物表，妻孔耋齒孀居，窶迫殘日，欽風撫事，嗟慨滿懷。

translations.literal: Shanyin's Zhu Bainian's Way ended beyond things; his wife Kong, in old widowhood, destitute in her remaining days—admiring virtue and touching affairs, sighing fills the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Bainian of Shanyin has passed beyond this world; his wife Kong, a widow in advanced age, lives in hardship through her last days. Thinking of their virtue moves me to sigh with full heart.

sentences.zh: 可以帳下米，各餉百斛。

translations.literal: May use granary rice; to each provide a hundred hu.
translations.idiomatic: You may draw from the prefectural granary and give each of them a hundred hu of rice.

sentences.zh: 」原平固讓頻煩，誓死不受。

translations.literal: Yuan Ping firmly declined repeatedly and swore he would die rather than accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ping refused again and again and swore he would rather die than accept.

sentences.zh: 人或問曰：「府君嘉君淳行，敏君貧老，故加此贍，豈宜必辭。

translations.literal: Someone asked, saying: "The prefect commends your pure conduct and pities your poverty and old age, therefore adding this support—how should one necessarily decline?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked him, "The prefect praises your pure conduct and pities your poverty and age, and so offers you this support. Why must you refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」原平曰：「府君若以吾義行邪，則無一介之善，不可濫荷此賜。

translations.literal: Yuan Ping said: "If the prefect considers my righteous conduct, then I have not one minuscule good deed and cannot recklessly bear this gift."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ping said, "If the prefect is rewarding my conduct, I have done nothing worthy of note and cannot accept such a gift unearned."

sentences.zh: 若以其貧老邪，耋齒甚多，屢空比室，非吾一人而已。

translations.literal: If because of poverty and old age, aged teeth are very many and empty kitchens neighbor by neighbor—it is not I alone.
translations.idiomatic: If it is because I am poor and old, there are many others of advanced age with empty larders in every house nearby—not I alone.

sentences.zh: 」終不肯納。

translations.literal: In the end he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he would not take it.

sentences.zh: 百年妻亦辭不受。

translations.literal: Bainian's wife also declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Bainian's widow also refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 會稽貴重望計及望孝，盛族出身，不減秘、著。

translations.literal: Kuaiji highly valued Wangji and Wangxiao; prominent clan origins were not less than the Secretariat and the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Kuaiji the honorary posts of Wangji and Wangxiao were greatly prized, and candidates from eminent clans were held in esteem no less than those from secretarial and historiographical families.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始七年，興宗欲舉山陰孔仲智長子為望計，原平次息為望孝。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi under Emperor Taizong, Xingzong wished to recommend Kong Zhongzhi's eldest son of Shanyin as Wangji and Yuan Ping's second son as Wangxiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Taishi era, Cai Xingzong wished to nominate Kong Zhongzhi's eldest son of Shanyin for Wangji and Yuan Ping's second son for Wangxiao.

sentences.zh: 仲智會土高門，原平一邦至行，欲以相敵。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi was a high gate of Kuaiji soil; Yuan Ping was the commandery's utmost conduct—they wished to match each other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi came from a great Kuaiji family, and Yuan Ping was the most exemplary man in the commandery; Xingzong wanted the two nominations to be equally matched.

sentences.zh: 會太宗別敕用人，故二選並寢。

translations.literal: As Emperor Taizong separately decreed the use of personnel, therefore both selections were shelved.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor issued a separate decree on appointments, and both nominations were set aside.

sentences.zh: 泰豫元年，興宗徵還京師，表其殊行，宜舉拔顯選，以勸風俗。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiyu, Xingzong was recalled to the capital and memorialized Yuan Ping's extraordinary conduct, saying he should be recommended for prominent selection to encourage custom.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiyu, Xingzong was recalled to the capital and memorialized Yuan Ping's extraordinary conduct, urging that he be promoted to a distinguished post to encourage the people.

sentences.zh: 舉為太學博士。

translations.literal: He was recommended as Grand Academy erudite.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ping was recommended as an erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 會興宗薨，事不行。

translations.literal: As Xingzong died, the matter did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: But Xingzong died before the appointment could be made, and the matter came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 明年，元徽元年，卒於家。

translations.literal: The next year, the first year of Yuanhui, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, the first year of Yuanhui, he died at home.

sentences.zh: 原平少長交物，無忤辭於人，與其居處者數十年，未嘗見喜慍之色。

translations.literal: Yuan Ping from youth to age in dealing with others had no offending words toward people; with those he lived for decades, one never saw joy or anger on his face.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to old age Yuan Ping dealt with others without giving offense, and those who lived near him for decades never once saw joy or anger on his face.

sentences.zh: 三子一弟，並有門行。

translations.literal: Three sons and one younger brother—all had family conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His three sons and one younger brother all upheld the family's reputation for virtue.

sentences.zh: 長子伯林，舉孝廉，次子靈馥，儒林祭酒，皆不就。

translations.literal: The eldest son Bolin was recommended as filial and incorrupt; the second son Lingfu was appointed Libationer of the Confucian Forest—all did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Bolin was recommended as filial and incorrupt, and his second son Lingfu was offered the post of Libationer of the Confucian Forest—but both declined.

sentences.zh: 嚴世期，會稽山陰人也。

translations.literal: Yan Shiqi was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shiqi was a native of Shanyin in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 好施慕善，出自天然。

translations.literal: He loved giving and admired goodness—it came from nature itself.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to give and admired goodness; it came naturally to him.

sentences.zh: 同里張邁三人，妻各產子，時歲饑儉，慮不相存，欲棄而不舉。

translations.literal: Three men of the same hamlet, the Zhang brothers, each had wives who bore sons; at the time the year was famine and dearth, fearing they could not survive, they wished to abandon and not raise them.
translations.idiomatic: Three brothers surnamed Zhang in his hamlet each had wives who gave birth; famine was severe that year, and fearing they could not keep their children alive, they meant to abandon the infants.

sentences.zh: 世期聞之，馳往拯救，分食解衣，以贍其乏，三子並得成長。

translations.literal: Shiqi heard and galloped to save them, dividing food and giving clothes to relieve their want; all three sons grew to adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiqi heard of this, he rushed to intervene, sharing food and giving clothes to relieve their need, and all three children grew up.

sentences.zh: 同縣俞陽妻莊年九十，莊女蘭七十，並各老病，單孤無所依，世期衣飴之二十餘年，死並殯葬。

translations.literal: In the same county, Yu Yang's wife Zhuang was ninety years old and Zhuang's daughter Lan was seventy; each was old and ill, alone and orphaned with none to rely on. Shiqi clothed and fed them for more than twenty years, and when they died he coffined and buried them both.
translations.idiomatic: In the same county, Yu Yang's wife Zhuang was ninety and her daughter Lan was seventy; both were old and ill, alone with no one to depend on. Shiqi clothed and fed them for more than twenty years, and when they died he saw to their burial.

sentences.zh: 宗親嚴弘、鄉人潘伯等十五人，荒年並餓死，露骸不收，世期買棺器殯埋，存育孩幼。

translations.literal: Clansmen Yan Hong, village man Pan Bo, and fifteen others in bad years all starved to death; exposed corpses were uncollected. Shiqi bought coffins and buried them, and preserved and raised the infants.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen people, including his kinsman Yan Hong and his neighbor Pan Bo, starved to death in years of famine, their bodies left unburied. Shiqi bought coffins and buried them, and took in and raised the children who were left.

sentences.zh: 山陰令何曼之表言之。

translations.literal: Shanyin magistrate He Manzhi memorialized about it.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Shanyin, He Manzhi, reported his deeds to the throne.

sentences.zh: 元嘉四年，有司奏榜門曰：「義行嚴氏之閭」，復其身徭役，蠲租稅十年。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanjia, the responsible offices memorialized to honor the gate with the inscription "Righteous conduct of the Yan clan's lane," restored his personal corvée, and exempted rent and tax for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanjia, the authorities memorialized that his gate be honored with the inscription "The Lane of the Yan Clan's Righteous Conduct," his corvée duties remitted, and his rent and taxes waived for ten years.

sentences.zh: 吳逵，吳興烏程人也。

translations.literal: Wu Da was a man of Wucheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Da was a native of Wucheng in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 經荒饑饉，係以疾疫，父母兄弟嫂及群從小功之親，男女死者十三人。

translations.literal: Enduring famine and dearth, followed by pestilence—parents, brothers, sister-in-law, and close kin of lesser mourning grade, men and women dead, thirteen persons.
translations.idiomatic: After famine and plague swept the land, thirteen relatives died—his parents, brothers, sister-in-law, and other close kin of the lesser mourning grades, men and women together.

sentences.zh: 逵時病困，鄰里以葦席裹之，埋於村側。

translations.literal: Da was then ill and confined; neighbors wrapped him in a reed mat and buried him at the village side.
translations.idiomatic: Da himself lay gravely ill; the neighbors wrapped him in a reed mat and buried him at the edge of the village, thinking him dead.

sentences.zh: 既而逵疾得瘳，親屬皆盡，唯逵夫妻獲全。

translations.literal: Before long Da's illness recovered; relatives were all gone—only Da and his wife were fully preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Da recovered from his illness, but all his relatives were gone; only he and his wife survived.

sentences.zh: 家徒壁立，冬無被絝，晝則庸賃，夜則伐木燒磚，此誠無有懈倦。

translations.literal: The house was bare as walls; in winter there were no quilts or trousers. By day he hired out his labor; by night he felled wood and burned brick—truly without slack or weariness.
translations.idiomatic: His home was utterly bare; in winter he had no quilt or trousers. By day he hired himself out for wages; by night he cut wood and fired bricks—and he never slackened.

sentences.zh: 逵夜行遇虎，虎輒下道避之。

translations.literal: Da walking at night encountered a tiger; the tiger always left the road to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: When Da walked at night and met a tiger, the tiger always left the path to avoid him.

sentences.zh: 期年中，成七墓，葬十三棺。

translations.literal: Within the year he completed seven tombs and buried thirteen coffins.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he had built seven tombs and buried thirteen coffins.

sentences.zh: 鄰里嘉其志義，葬日悉出赴助，送終之事，亦儉而周禮。

translations.literal: Neighbors praised his resolve and righteousness; on the burial day all came out to help, and the send-off affairs were also frugal yet complete in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The neighbors admired his devotion; on the burial days they all came to help, and though the funerals were frugal, every rite was properly observed.

sentences.zh: 逵時逆取鄰人夫直，葬畢，眾悉以施之；

translations.literal: Da then borrowed ahead the neighbors' labor wages; when the burial was finished, all wished to give them to him;
translations.idiomatic: Da had borrowed his neighbors' wages in advance for the burials, and when the work was done they all offered the money to him;

sentences.zh: 逵一無所受，皆傭力報答焉。

translations.literal: Da absolutely would not accept any and repaid all by hired labor.
translations.idiomatic: but he refused every penny and repaid them all with his own labor.

sentences.zh: 太守張崇之三加禮命，太守王韶之擢補功曹史，逵以門寒，固辭不就，舉為孝廉。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhang Chongzhi thrice added ceremonial appointment; Prefect Wang Shaozhi promoted him to supplement Clerk for Merit—Da because his family was humble firmly declined and did not accept; he was recommended as filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Chongzhi repeatedly offered him official honors; Prefect Wang Shaozhi wished to appoint him clerk for merit—but Da, citing his humble origins, firmly declined. He was nevertheless recommended as filial and incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 潘綜，吳興烏程人也。

translations.literal: Pan Zong was a man of Wucheng in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zong was a native of Wucheng in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 孫恩之亂，妖黨攻破村邑，綜與父驃共走避賊。

translations.literal: In Sun En's rebellion, demonic factions broke villages and towns; Zong and his father Biao together fled to avoid the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: During Sun En's rebellion, rebel bands overran the villages, and Zong fled with his father Biao to escape them.

sentences.zh: 驃年老行遲，賊轉逼，驃語綜：「我不能去，汝走可脫，幸勿俱死。

translations.literal: Biao was old and walked slowly; the bandits pressed closer. Biao told Zong: "I cannot go; you run and can escape—do not hope to die together."
translations.idiomatic: Biao was old and could not move quickly; the rebels were closing in. He said to Zong, "I cannot get away. You run—you may escape. Please do not die with me."

sentences.zh: 」驃困乏坐地，綜迎賊叩頭曰：「父年老，乞賜生命。

translations.literal: Biao, exhausted, sat on the ground. Zong met the bandits and knocked his head, saying: "Father is old—beg grant life."
translations.idiomatic: Biao, exhausted, sank to the ground. Zong went to meet the rebels and kowtowed, saying, "My father is old—I beg you to spare his life."

sentences.zh: 」賊至，驃亦請賊曰：「兒年少，自能走，今為老子不走去。

translations.literal: The bandits arrived; Biao also asked the bandits: "The boy is young and can run himself—now for this old man he will not leave."
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived, Biao also pleaded with them: "My son is young and could escape, but he refuses to leave me behind."

sentences.zh: 老子不惜死，乞活此兒。

translations.literal: This old man does not begrudge death—beg spare this boy.
translations.idiomatic: I do not begrudge my own death—please spare this boy.

sentences.zh: 」賊因斫驃，綜抱父於腹下，賊斫綜頭面，凡四創，綜當時悶絕。

translations.literal: The bandits therefore hacked Biao; Zong embraced his father under his belly; the bandits hacked Zong's head and face—four wounds in all—and Zong then fainted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hacked at Biao; Zong shielded his father with his body. They slashed Zong's head and face four times, and he fainted on the spot.

sentences.zh: 有一賊從傍來，相謂曰：「卿欲舉大事，此兒以死救父，云何可殺。

translations.literal: One bandit came from the side and said to the others: "You wish to raise a great affair—this boy with his death saves his father; how can he be killed?"
translations.idiomatic: One rebel came up beside them and said to the others, "You mean to accomplish great things—this boy is ready to die for his father. How can you kill him?"

sentences.zh: 殺孝子不祥。

translations.literal: To kill a filial son is ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: To kill a filial son brings ill fortune.

sentences.zh: 」賊良久乃止，父子並得免。

translations.literal: After a long while the bandits then stopped; father and son both escaped.
translations.idiomatic: After a long moment the rebels stopped, and father and son both survived.

sentences.zh: 綜鄉人秘書監丘繼祖、廷尉沈赤黔以綜異行，廉補左民令史，除遂昌長，歲滿還家。

translations.literal: Zong's fellow townsman Secretary Supervisor Qiu Jizu and Court Director Shen Chiqian, because of Zong's extraordinary conduct, fairly supplemented him as Clerk of the Left People; he was removed as magistrate of Suichang, and when his term was fulfilled he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's fellow townsman Qiu Jizu, Director of the Secretariat, and Shen Chiqian, Director of the Court of Justice, recognizing his extraordinary conduct, had him appointed clerk in the Left People Office. He later served as magistrate of Suichang, and when his term ended he returned home.

sentences.zh: 太守王韶之臨郡，發教曰：「前被符，孝廉之選，必審其人，雖四科難該，文質寡備，必能孝義邁俗，拔萃著聞者，便足以顯應明易攵，允將符旨。

translations.literal: Prefect Wang Shaozhi came to the commandery and issued an instruction, saying: "Previously we received a dispatch: in selecting filial and incorrupt candidates one must examine the person closely. Though the four categories are hard to cover completely and literary and substance are rarely both present, one who can in filial piety and righteousness surpass custom and stand out with renown suffices to manifest response to enlightened government and truly accord with the dispatch's intent."
translations.idiomatic: When Prefect Wang Shaozhi arrived in the commandery, he issued an instruction: "We have received orders that candidates for filial and incorrupt office must be carefully vetted. Though few meet every standard of talent and character, anyone whose filial piety and righteousness clearly surpass ordinary men and whose reputation stands out is enough to fulfill the enlightened policy behind the decree and honor its intent."

sentences.zh: 烏程潘綜守死孝道，全親濟難。

translations.literal: Wucheng's Pan Zong guarded unto death the filial Way and preserved his parent through peril.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zong of Wucheng held fast to filial duty even unto death and saved his father in peril.

sentences.zh: 烏程吳逵義行純至，列墳成行。

translations.literal: Wucheng's Wu Da had righteous conduct pure and utmost; a row of tombs formed a line.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Da of Wucheng showed pure and perfect righteousness, burying his kin in a row of graves.

sentences.zh: 咸精誠內淳，休聲外著，可並察孝廉，並列上州台，陳其行跡。

translations.literal: All have sincerity inner and pure and fine reputation outwardly manifest—they may both be inspected as filial and incorrupt, jointly listed upward to the province and platform, and their tracks stated.
translations.idiomatic: Both are sincere within and renowned without. They should be nominated together as filial and incorrupt candidates, reported to the provincial authorities, and their deeds set forth in full.

sentences.zh: 」及將行，設祖道，贈以四言詩曰：

translations.literal: When they were about to depart, he set a farewell feast and gifted them with four-character verse, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When they were about to leave, he held a farewell feast and presented them with a poem in four-character lines:

sentences.zh: 東寶惟金，南木有喬。

translations.literal: East's treasure is gold; south's trees have loftiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the east, treasure is gold; in the south, trees grow tall.

sentences.zh: 發輝曾崖，竦幹重霄。

translations.literal: Sending radiance from layered cliffs, towering trunks reach heavy sky.
translations.idiomatic: They shine from lofty cliffs; their towering trunks reach the heavens.

sentences.zh: 美哉茲土，世載英髦。

translations.literal: Beautiful is this land; generations carry heroic talent.
translations.idiomatic: How fine is this land—generation after generation it produces men of excellence.

sentences.zh: 育翮幽林，養音九皋。

translations.literal: Nurturing pinions in dark forest, cultivating voice in nine marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Wings are nurtured in hidden groves; voices are cultivated across the distant marshlands.

sentences.zh: 其一

translations.literal: The first.
translations.idiomatic: I.

sentences.zh: 唐後明易攵，漢宗蒲輪。

translations.literal: After Yao, enlightened governance; the Han house, pu-wheeled chariots.
translations.idiomatic: After the age of Yao came enlightened rule; under the Han, worthies were summoned in chariots with wheels wrapped in rush.

sentences.zh: 我皇降鑒，思樂懷人。

translations.literal: Our emperor descends scrutiny; thinking joy, he cherishes such men.
translations.idiomatic: Our emperor looks down in judgment and delights in cherishing men of worth.

sentences.zh: 群臣競薦，舊章惟新。

translations.literal: Ministers compete to recommend; old statutes are made new.
translations.idiomatic: Officials vie to recommend the worthy, and ancient institutions are renewed.

sentences.zh: 余亦奚貢，曰義與仁。

translations.literal: I too what tribute? I say righteousness and benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: What can I offer in turn? Righteousness and benevolence.

sentences.zh: 其二

translations.literal: The second.
translations.idiomatic: II.

sentences.zh: 仁義伊在，惟吳惟潘。

translations.literal: Benevolence and righteousness are here—only Wu, only Pan.
translations.idiomatic: Here stand benevolence and righteousness—in Wu and in Pan.

sentences.zh: 心積純孝，事著艱難。

translations.literal: Hearts accumulated pure filial piety; deeds shown in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Their hearts are steeped in pure filial devotion; their deeds were proved in hardship.

sentences.zh: 投死如歸，淑問若蘭。

translations.literal: Throwing oneself toward death like returning home; fine fame like orchid.
translations.idiomatic: They faced death as calmly as going home; their good repute is fragrant as orchid.

sentences.zh: 吳實履仁，心力偕單。

translations.literal: Wu in truth treads benevolence; heart and strength together single.
translations.idiomatic: Wu truly lived benevolence, giving all his heart and strength alone.

sentences.zh: 固此苦節，易彼歲寒。

translations.literal: Fixing this bitter integrity changes that cold of year.
translations.idiomatic: Such steadfast integrity transforms the chill of hard times.

sentences.zh: 霜雪雖厚，松柏丸丸。

translations.literal: Frost and snow though thick, pine and cypress round and full.
translations.idiomatic: Though frost and snow lie deep, pine and cypress stand firm and full.

sentences.zh: 其三

translations.literal: The third.
translations.idiomatic: III.

sentences.zh: 人亦有言，無善不彰。

translations.literal: Men also have a saying: no goodness is not displayed.
translations.idiomatic: As the saying goes, no good deed goes unremarked.

sentences.zh: 二子徽猷，彌久彌芳。

translations.literal: The two sons' fine virtue—more long, more fragrant.
translations.idiomatic: These two men's fine conduct grows more fragrant with time.

sentences.zh: 拔叢出類，景行朝陽。

translations.literal: Plucked from thicket, out from the kind—sunlit conduct at the dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Raised above the common crowd, their shining conduct faces the morning sun.

sentences.zh: 誰謂道遐，弘之則光。

translations.literal: Who says the Way is far? Extend it and it shines.
translations.idiomatic: Who says the Way is distant? Broaden it and it shines forth.

sentences.zh: 咨爾庶士，無然怠荒。

translations.literal: Consult you common scholars—be not thus slack and wasteful.
translations.idiomatic: Take heed, you common scholars—do not grow idle and neglect your duty.

sentences.zh: 其四

translations.literal: The fourth.
translations.idiomatic: IV.

sentences.zh: 江革奉摯，慶祿是荷。

translations.literal: Jiang Ge bore the bundle; blessed emolument is what he carried.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ge carried his mother on his back; such is the honored burden of filial reward.

sentences.zh: 姜詩入貢，漢朝咨嗟。

translations.literal: Jiang Shi entered tribute; the Han court sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shi presented his tribute; the Han court marveled in admiration.

sentences.zh: 勖哉行人，敬爾休嘉。

translations.literal: Exhort you travelers—revere your fine excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Press on, you who go forth, and honor the fine virtue you bear.

sentences.zh: 俾是下國，照輝京華。

translations.literal: Make this lower state shine and illume the capital splendor.
translations.idiomatic: May this humble region send forth light to brighten the imperial capital.

sentences.zh: 其五

translations.literal: The fifth.
translations.idiomatic: V.

sentences.zh: 伊餘朽駘，竊服懼盜。

translations.literal: I, decayed and feeble, secretly revere yet fear theft.
translations.idiomatic: I am old and worn, and though I admire them, I fear to steal undeserved praise.

sentences.zh: 無能禮樂，豈暇聲教。

translations.literal: Unable in rites and music—how could I spare time for vocal instruction?
translations.idiomatic: Unskilled in rites and music, how could I presume to offer learned counsel?

sentences.zh: 順彼康夷，懿德是好。

translations.literal: Following those peaceful and easy, fine virtue is what I love.
translations.idiomatic: I can only follow their tranquil grace and honor their splendid virtue.

sentences.zh: 聊綴所懷，以贈二孝。

translations.literal: Briefly string together what is in my heart, to gift the two filial ones.
translations.idiomatic: I bind up these humble feelings and offer them to the two filial sons.

sentences.zh: 其六

translations.literal: The sixth.
translations.idiomatic: VI.

sentences.zh: 元嘉四年，有司奏改其里為純孝里，蠲租布三世。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanjia, the offices memorialized to change his hamlet to Chunxiao Hamlet, remitting rent and cloth for three generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanjia, the authorities memorialized the court to rename his hamlet Pure Filial Hamlet and exempt his family from rent and cloth taxes for three generations.

sentences.zh: 張進之，永嘉安固人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jinzhi was a man of Angu in Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jinzhi was a native of Angu in Yongjia commandery.

sentences.zh: 為郡大族。

translations.literal: He was a great clan of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His family was one of the commandery's great clans.

sentences.zh: 少有志行，歷郡五官主簿，永寧、安固二縣領校尉。

translations.literal: In youth he had resolve and conduct; he served as Five Offices chief clerk of the commandery, and district commandant of Yongning and Angu counties.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he showed resolve and integrity; he served as chief clerk of the commandery's Five Offices and as district commandant of Yongning and Angu counties.

sentences.zh: 家世富足，經荒年散其財，救贍鄉里，遂以貧罄，全濟者甚多。

translations.literal: His family for generations was wealthy; during a famine year he dispersed his wealth to relieve and support the village, and thereby became utterly poor—those fully saved were very many.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long been wealthy, but in years of famine he gave away his fortune to feed his neighbors, leaving himself utterly destitute while saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 進之為太守王味之吏，味之有罪當見收，逃避投進之家，供奉經時，盡其誠力。

translations.literal: Jinzhi was clerk to Prefect Wang Weizhi; Weizhi had a crime and should be arrested; fleeing, he came to Jinzhi's home; Jinzhi supported him for a long time, exhausting his sincerity and strength.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhi had served as clerk to Prefect Wang Weizhi. When Weizhi was charged with a crime and faced arrest, he fled to Jinzhi's home. Jinzhi supported him for a long while and gave all he could.

sentences.zh: 以本村淺近，移入池溪，味之墮水沈沒，進之投水拯救，相與沈淪，危而得免。

translations.literal: Because the home village was shallow and close, they moved to Chixi; Weizhi fell into the water and sank; Jinzhi threw himself into the water to rescue him; together they sank, yet in peril escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Because their village was too exposed, they moved to Chixi. Weizhi fell into the water and sank; Jinzhi plunged in after him. Both went under, but in the end they survived.

sentences.zh: 時劫掠充斥，每入村抄暴，至進之門，輒相約勒，不得侵犯，其信義所感如此。

translations.literal: At the time plundering filled the land; whenever they entered villages to loot and ravage, arriving at Jinzhi's gate they always made mutual pacts to restrain one another and not violate it—such was how his faith and righteousness moved them.
translations.idiomatic: In those days bandits ravaged the countryside, but whenever they came to Jinzhi's gate they agreed among themselves not to harm him—such was the power of his integrity.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，詔在所蠲其徭役。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanjia, an edict at the place remitted his corvée and labor service.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanjia era, an edict exempted him from corvée labor wherever he lived.

sentences.zh: 孫恩之亂，永嘉太守司馬逸之被害，妻子並死，兵寇之際，莫敢收藏。

translations.literal: In the rebellion of Sun En, Yongjia Prefect Sima Yizhi was killed; wife and children both died; amid soldiers and bandits, none dared to gather the bodies.
translations.idiomatic: During Sun En's rebellion, Yongjia Prefect Sima Yizhi was killed along with his wife and children. In the chaos of war no one dared bury them.

sentences.zh: 郡吏俞僉以家財買棺斂逸之等六喪，送致還都，葬畢乃歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Commandery clerk Yu Qian used family wealth to buy coffins and bury Yizhi and the other six dead, sent them back to the capital, and after burial returned to his village.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery clerk Yu Qian spent his own money to buy coffins and bury Yizhi and five others, then sent the remains back to the capital. Only after the burials were complete did he return home.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，老病卒。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era, old and ill, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died of old age and illness during the Yuanjia era.

sentences.zh: 王彭，盱眙直瀆人也。

translations.literal: Wang Peng was a man of Zhidu in Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Peng was a native of Zhidu in Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 少喪母。

translations.literal: In youth he lost his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his mother in youth.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，父又喪亡，家貧力弱，無以營葬，兄弟二人，晝則傭力，夜則號感。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanjia, his father also died; the family was poor and strength weak; there was no means to arrange burial; the two brothers by day hired out labor, by night wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanjia his father died as well. The family was poor and weak, with no means for a burial. The two brothers hired themselves out by day and grieved aloud through the night.

sentences.zh: 鄉里並哀之，乃各出夫力助作磚。

translations.literal: The village all pitied them and each contributed labor to help make bricks.
translations.idiomatic: The villagers took pity on them and each sent men to help make burial bricks.

sentences.zh: 磚須水而天旱，穿井數十丈，泉不出；

translations.literal: Bricks require water, but Heaven droughted; they dug a well several tens of zhang, yet no spring came forth;
translations.idiomatic: Bricks need water, but the land was drought-stricken; they dug a well tens of feet deep, yet no water appeared.

sentences.zh: 墓處去淮五里，荷檐遠汲，困而不周。

translations.literal: The grave site was five li from the Huai; carrying pole-buckets, drawing from afar—they were exhausted and could not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: The grave lay five li from the Huai River, and hauling water on shoulder poles from so far left them exhausted and short.

sentences.zh: 彭號天自訴，如此積日。

translations.literal: Peng cried out to Heaven in self-appeal, thus for accumulated days.
translations.idiomatic: Peng cried out to Heaven day after day in anguish.

sentences.zh: 一旦大霧，霧歇，磚灶前忽生泉水，鄉鄰助之者，並嗟歎神異，縣邑近遠，悉往觀之。

translations.literal: One morning great fog; when the fog cleared, before the brick kiln a spring suddenly appeared; neighbors who had helped all sighed in wonder at the divine marvel; near and far in the county all went to look.
translations.idiomatic: One morning a great fog rolled in, and when it lifted a spring suddenly welled up before the brick kiln. All who had helped marveled at the miracle, and people came from near and far throughout the county to see it.

sentences.zh: 葬事既竟，水便自竭。

translations.literal: When the burial affairs were finished, the water then dried up of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Once the burial was complete, the spring dried up on its own.

sentences.zh: 元嘉九年，太守劉伯龍依事表言，改其里為通靈里，蠲租布三世。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanjia, Prefect Liu Bolong according to the matter memorialized, changing his hamlet to Tongling Hamlet, remitting rent and cloth for three generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanjia, Prefect Liu Bolong memorialized the court, and his hamlet was renamed Spirit-Responsive Hamlet with three generations exempt from rent and cloth taxes.

sentences.zh: 蔣恭，義興臨津人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Gong was a man of Linjin in Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Gong was a native of Linjin in Yixing.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，晉陵蔣崇平為劫見禽，云與恭妻弟吳晞張為侶。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era, Jinling's Jiang Chongping was captured as a bandit, saying he was partner with Gong's wife's younger brother Wu Xizhang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanjia era, Jiang Chongping of Jinling was caught as a bandit and said he had acted with Gong's brother-in-law Wu Xizhang.

sentences.zh: 晞張先行不在，本村遇水，妻息五口避水移寄恭家，討錄晞張不獲，收恭及兄協付獄治罪。

translations.literal: Xizhang had gone ahead and was not present; in the home village they encountered flood; wife and children, five mouths, moved to take shelter at Gong's home; seeking to capture Xizhang without success, they arrested Gong and his elder brother Xie and delivered them to prison for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Xizhang was away at the time. When flooding struck their village, his wife and five children took refuge in Gong's home. Unable to capture Xizhang, the authorities arrested Gong and his elder brother Xie and imprisoned them.

sentences.zh: 恭、協並款舍住晞張家口，而不知劫情。

translations.literal: Gong and Xie both honestly admitted sheltering Xizhang's household, yet did not know of the banditry.
translations.idiomatic: Gong and Xie both admitted honestly that Xizhang's family had stayed with them, but said they knew nothing of the robbery.

sentences.zh: 恭列晞張妻息是婦之親，親今有罪，恭身甘分，求遣兄協。

translations.literal: Gong stated that Xizhang's wife and children were his wife's kin; now that kin had a crime, Gong himself would gladly bear the penalty and asked that elder brother Xie be sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Gong declared that Xizhang's wife and children were his wife's relatives; since those kin were guilty, he would gladly accept punishment himself and asked that his elder brother Xie be released.

sentences.zh: 協列協是戶主，延制所由，有罪之日，關協而已，救遣弟恭。

translations.literal: Xie stated that Xie was head of household and the cause of the extended shelter; on the day of guilt, only Xie was involved—he asked that younger brother Gong be sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Xie argued that as head of household he was responsible for taking them in; when guilt was incurred, only he should be implicated, and he asked that his younger brother Gong be released.

sentences.zh: 兄弟二人，爭求受罪，郡縣不能判，依事上詳。

translations.literal: The two brothers both vied to seek punishment; commandery and county could not decide, and according to the matter sent up for detailed report.
translations.idiomatic: The two brothers each insisted on taking the blame; the local authorities could not decide and reported the case upward.

sentences.zh: 州議之曰：「禮讓者以義為先，自厚者以利為上，末世俗薄，靡不自私。

translations.literal: The province deliberated, saying: "Courtesy and yielding take righteousness as first; self-enrichment takes profit as supreme—in this age's shallow customs, none do not act for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The province deliberated: "In courtesy and yielding, righteousness comes first; in self-advancement, profit comes first. In these shallow times, who does not act for himself?"

sentences.zh: 伏膺聖教，猶或不逮，況在野夫，未達誥訓，而能互發天倫之憂，甘受莫測之罪，若斯情義，實為殊特。

translations.literal: Bearing the sage's teaching on the breast, some still do not reach it—how much more for men of the wilds, who have not attained the proclamations and instructions, yet can mutually stir heavenly kin's sorrow and gladly accept immeasurable guilt—if such sentiment and righteousness, truly it is exceptionally rare.
translations.idiomatic: Even those who embrace the sage's teaching often fall short—how much more country folk who have never heard the court's edicts, yet can rouse such brotherly devotion and willingly face unknown punishment. Such loyalty is truly extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 蔑爾恭、協，而能行之，茲乃終古之所希，盛世之嘉事。

translations.literal: Humble though Gong and Xie are, yet able to act thus—this is what all antiquity has rarely seen, a fine affair of a flourishing age.
translations.idiomatic: Humble men though Gong and Xie may be, that they could act thus is what all antiquity has rarely seen—a glory of a flourishing age.

sentences.zh: 二子乘舟，無以過此。

translations.literal: The two sons in the boat—nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Like the two sons in the boat of old—nothing can surpass this.

sentences.zh: 豈宜拘執憲文，加以罪戮！

translations.literal: How can one rigidly hold to the letter of law and add punishment and execution!
translations.idiomatic: How can one cling to the letter of the law and punish men such as these!

sentences.zh: 且晞張封筒遠行，他界為劫，造釁自外，贓不還家，所寓村伍，容有不知，不合加罪。

translations.literal: Moreover Xizhang sealed his bundle and traveled far; in another district he committed robbery—the offense arose from outside; the stolen goods did not return home; the village where they lodged may have been unknowing—one should not add guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Xizhang had left on a distant journey and committed robbery elsewhere; the crime originated outside, the loot never came home, and the village that sheltered his family could not have known—guilt should not be imputed.

sentences.zh: 」勒縣遣之，還復民伍。

translations.literal: They ordered the county to release them and restore them to the common register.
translations.idiomatic: The province ordered the county to release them and restore them to the common register.

sentences.zh: 乃除恭義成令，協義怡令。

translations.literal: Then Gong was made Magistrate of Yicheng, Xie Magistrate of Yiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was then appointed Magistrate of Yicheng and Xie Magistrate of Yiyi.

sentences.zh: 徐耕，晉陵延陵人也。

translations.literal: Xu Geng was a man of Yanling in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Geng was a native of Yanling in Jinling.

sentences.zh: 自令史除平原令。

translations.literal: From clerk he was removed to be magistrate of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from clerk to become magistrate of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十一年，大旱民饑，耕詣縣陳辭曰：「今年亢旱，禾稼不登。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, great drought and the people starved; Geng went to the county and stated in memorial: "This year severe drought—the grain crops did not ripen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, a great drought brought famine. Geng went to the county seat and petitioned: "This year the drought is severe and the crops have failed.

sentences.zh: 氓黎饑餒，采掇存命，聖上哀矜，已垂存拯。

translations.literal: The common folk hunger and starve, gathering and plucking to preserve life; the sage above pities, already letting down preservation and rescue.
translations.idiomatic: The people are starving and scraping together whatever they can to survive. His Majesty has already shown pity and ordered relief.

sentences.zh: 但饉罄來久，困殆者眾，米穀轉貴，糴索元所。

translations.literal: But famine exhaustion has come long; the trapped and endangered are many; rice and grain turn expensive; to purchase grain there is nowhere.
translations.idiomatic: But hunger has persisted for so long that many are at the point of collapse; grain grows ever costlier and there is nowhere to buy it.

sentences.zh: 方涉春夏，日月悠長，不有微救，永無濟理。

translations.literal: Now spanning spring and summer, days and months long and lingering—without slight rescue, forever no means of salvation.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and summer stretch long before the harvest; without immediate aid, there will be no saving them.

sentences.zh: 不惟凡瑣，敢憂身外，《鹿鳴》之求，思同野草，氣類之感，能不傷心。

translations.literal: Not only trivial matters—dare I worry beyond the body? The Deer Call's seeking thinks the same as wild grass; kindred breath's feeling—can one not be wounded in heart?
translations.idiomatic: I do not speak of trifles alone, but of lives at stake. As in the "Deer Call," I feel for the people as for withered grass on the plain—how can the heart not break?

sentences.zh: 民糴得少米，資供朝夕。

translations.literal: The people purchasing obtained a little rice to supply morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: The people can buy only a little rice to sustain themselves from day to day.

sentences.zh: 志欲自竭，義存分飧，今以千斛，助官賑貸。

translations.literal: My will is to exhaust myself; righteousness lies in sharing a meal—now with a thousand hu I assist the office in relief lending.
