translations.idiomatic: I wish to give all I can, for righteousness lies in sharing one's food. I now offer a thousand hu to aid the county in relief.

sentences.zh: 此境連年不熟，今歲尤甚，晉陵境特為偏祐。

translations.literal: This territory for years in succession has not ripened; this year especially severe; the Jinling territory is especially hard hit.
translations.idiomatic: This region has failed to harvest for years, and this year is worst of all; Jinling has been hit especially hard.

sentences.zh: 此郡雖弊，猶有富室，承陂之家，處處而是，並皆保熟，所失蓋微。

translations.literal: This commandery though impoverished still has wealthy houses; families by the embankment are everywhere, all preserving ripeness—the loss is slight.
translations.idiomatic: Though this commandery is poor, wealthy households remain; families along the dikes have kept their crops safe and would lose little.

sentences.zh: 陳積之穀，皆有巨萬，旱之所弊，實鐘貧民，溫富之家，各有財寶。

translations.literal: Chen's stored grain all has tens of thousands; what drought harms truly falls on the poor folk; warm and wealthy families each have treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Those who store grain by the cartload have fortunes in the tens of thousands; drought strikes the poor hardest, while well-to-do families still have their wealth.

sentences.zh: 謂此等並宜助官，得過儉月，所損至輕，所濟甚重。

translations.literal: I say these sorts all should assist the office, getting through the lean months—the loss is very light, the relief very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: I urge such families to assist the authorities through the lean months—the loss to them would be slight, the benefit to the people immense.

sentences.zh: 今敢自勵，為勸造之端。

translations.literal: Now I dare encourage myself, making the beginning of exhortation and creation.
translations.idiomatic: I dare take the lead myself, hoping others will follow.

sentences.zh: 實願掘水揚塵，崇益山海。

translations.literal: Truly I wish to scoop water and raise dust, exalting and adding to mountain and sea.
translations.idiomatic: I would scoop up water to raise dust, adding my mite to mountains and seas.

sentences.zh: 」縣為言上。

translations.literal: " The county for him spoke upward.
translations.idiomatic: The county forwarded his petition to the court.

sentences.zh: 當時議者以耕比漢卜式，詔書褒美，酬以縣令。

translations.literal: At the time deliberators compared Geng to Han's Bu Shi; an edict praised and beautified, rewarding him with a county magistracy.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries compared Geng to Bu Shi of Han; an imperial edict praised him and rewarded him with a magistracy.

sentences.zh: 大明八年，東土饑旱，東海嚴成、東莞王道蓋各以穀五百斛助官賑恤。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Daming, the eastern lands hungered and droughted; Donghai's Yan Cheng and Dongguan's Wang Daigai each with five hundred hu of grain assisted the office in relief and succor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Daming, famine and drought struck the eastern provinces; Yan Cheng of Donghai and Wang Daigai of Dongguan each contributed five hundred hu of grain to aid official relief.

sentences.zh: 孫法宗，吳興人也。

translations.literal: Sun Fazong was a man of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fazong was a native of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父遇亂被害，屍骸不收，母兄並餓死。

translations.literal: His father met chaos and was killed; the corpse was not gathered; mother and elder brother both starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: His father was killed in the turmoil and his body was never recovered; his mother and elder brother both starved to death.

sentences.zh: 法宗年小流迸，至年十六，方得還。

translations.literal: Fazong, young, fled scattered; reaching age sixteen, he finally returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fazong fled as a child; only at sixteen was he able to return.

sentences.zh: 單身勤苦，霜行草宿，營辦棺槨，造立塚墓，葬送母兄，儉而有禮。

translations.literal: Alone he toiled in bitterness, walking in frost and sleeping in grass; he arranged coffins and cases, built and established tombs and graves, buried and sent off mother and elder brother—frugal yet with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He labored alone through hardship, sleeping in the open; he prepared coffins, built tombs, and buried his mother and brother—frugally but with full propriety.

sentences.zh: 以父喪不測，於部境之內，尋求枯骨，刺血以灌之，如此者十餘年不獲，乃縗絰。

translations.literal: Because his father's death was uncertain, within the department territory he sought withered bones, pricking blood to pour upon them—thus for more than ten years without obtaining them, then he wore hemp mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father's death remained uncertain, he searched the district for bones, pricking his finger to drip blood upon them as a test—for more than ten years without success, he wore mourning garb throughout.

sentences.zh: 終身不娶，饋遺無所受。

translations.literal: All his life he did not marry; gifts and offerings he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He never married and refused all gifts offered to him.

sentences.zh: 世祖初，揚州辟為文學從事，不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shizu, Yangzhou recruited him as Literary Adjunct; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign, Yang Province recruited him as Literary Adjunct, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 范叔孫，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Fan Shusun was a man of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shusun was a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 少而仁厚，固窮濟急。

translations.literal: In youth he was benevolent and generous, firmly relieving the destitute and aiding the urgent.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was kind and generous, steadfast in helping the poor and those in crisis.

sentences.zh: 同里范法先父母兄弟七人，同時疫死，唯餘法先，病又危篤，喪屍經月不收。

translations.literal: In the same village, Fan Faxian's parents, brothers, and seven persons at one time died of pestilence; only Faxian remained; his illness again was critically grave; the dead bodies for a month were not gathered.
translations.idiomatic: In the same village, seven members of Fan Faxian's family—parents, brothers, and others—all died of plague at once; only Faxian survived, himself gravely ill, and the corpses lay unburied for a month.

sentences.zh: 叔孫悉備棺器，親為殯埋。

translations.literal: Shusun fully prepared coffins and vessels and personally performed burial.
translations.idiomatic: Shusun supplied coffins and personally saw to their burial.

sentences.zh: 又同里施淵夫疾病，父母死不殯；

translations.literal: Also in the same village, Shi Yuanfu was ill; his parents died and were not buried;
translations.idiomatic: In the same village, Shi Yuanfu fell ill and his parents died without burial;

sentences.zh: 又同里范苗父子並亡；

translations.literal: Also in the same village, Fan Miao, father and son, both died;
translations.idiomatic: In the same village, Fan Miao and his son both died;

sentences.zh: 又同里危敬宗家口六人俱得病，二人喪沒，親鄰畏遠，莫敢營視。

translations.literal: Also in the same village, Wei Jingzong's household of six persons all fell ill; two died and were lost; kin and neighbors feared distance and none dared to tend or look.
translations.idiomatic: In the same village, six members of Wei Jingzong's household fell ill; two died, and neighbors were too afraid to come near.

sentences.zh: 叔孫並殯葬，躬恤病者，並皆得全。

translations.literal: Shusun in each case buried and sent off, personally comforting the ill—and all were fully preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Shusun buried the dead and nursed the sick in every case, and all who survived were saved.

sentences.zh: 鄉曲貴其義行，莫有呼其名者。

translations.literal: The village and lanes honored his righteous conduct; none called him by his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: The neighborhood honored his conduct so deeply that none ever called him by his personal name.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝建初，除竟陵王國中軍將軍，不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojian of Shizu, he was made Central Army General of the Kingdom of Jingling; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiaojian era, he was appointed Central Army General of the Kingdom of Jingling, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 義興吳國夫，亦有義讓之美。

translations.literal: Yixing's Wu Guofu also had the beauty of righteous yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guofu of Yixing likewise showed the virtue of magnanimous forbearance.

sentences.zh: 人有竊其稻者，乃引還，為設酒食，以米送之。

translations.literal: When someone stole his rice, he led him back, set out wine and food, and with rice sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: When someone stole his rice, he brought the man back, set out food and wine, and sent him away with a gift of rice.

sentences.zh: 卜天與，吳興餘杭人也。

translations.literal: Bu Tianyu was a man of Yuhang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Tianyu was a native of Yuhang in Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 父名祖，有勇幹，徐赤將為餘杭令，祖依隨之。

translations.literal: His father's name was Zu; he had courage and capability; Xu Chijiang was magistrate of Yuhang, and Zu followed and attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: His father, named Zu, was a man of courage and ability; when Xu Chijiang served as magistrate of Yuhang, Zu followed him.

sentences.zh: 赤將死，高祖聞其有幹力，召補隊主，從征伐，封關中侯，歷二縣令。

translations.literal: When Chijiang died, the Founding Emperor heard he had capability and strength, summoned and supplemented him as squad chief; he followed campaigns, was enfeoffed as Marquis within the Passes, and served as magistrate of two counties.
translations.idiomatic: After Chijiang's death, Emperor Wu heard of his ability and appointed him squad chief; he followed the campaigns, was enfeoffed as Marquis within the Passes, and served as magistrate of two counties.

sentences.zh: 天與善射，弓力兼倍，容貌嚴正，笑不解顏。

translations.literal: Tianyu was skilled at archery; bow strength doubled; his appearance stern and upright—when smiling he did not unknit his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyu was a master archer whose bow drew twice the usual weight; his bearing was stern, and he scarcely ever smiled.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其舊將子，便教皇子射。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, because he was an old general's son, then taught the princes archery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu, knowing him as the son of an old general, had him teach the princes archery.

sentences.zh: 居累年，以白衣領東掖防關隊。

translations.literal: Dwelling accumulated years, as commoner he led the Eastern Gate garrison defense squad.
translations.idiomatic: After many years of service, he held the post of Eastern Gate garrison defense squad leader while still a commoner.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十七年，臧質救懸瓠，劉興祖守白石，並率所領隨之，虜退罷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, Zang Zhi rescued Xuancheng; Liu Xingzu defended Baishi—both led their commands following him; when the barbarians retreated, they were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, Zang Zhi relieved Xuancheng and Liu Xingzu held Baishi; Tianyu followed both campaigns, and when the enemy withdrew he was released from duty.

sentences.zh: 遷領輦後第一隊，撫恤士卒，甚得眾心。

translations.literal: He was transferred to lead the first squad behind the imperial carriage, comforting and tending soldiers—greatly obtaining the masses' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to lead the first squad of the imperial escort, treating his men with such care that he won their deep loyalty.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以為廣威將軍，領左細仗，兼帶營祿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was made General of Broad Might, leading the left fine guard, and concurrently commanded the camp stipends.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was made General of Broad Might, commanding the left fine guard and the camp stipends.

sentences.zh: 子伯宗，殿中將軍。

translations.literal: His son Bozong was Palace Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bozong served as Palace Guard General.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始初，領幢，擊南賊於赭圻，戰沒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi of Emperor Xiaoming, he led the banner guard and struck the southern rebels at Zheqi, dying in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taishi era, he led the banner guard and fought the southern rebels at Zheqi, where he fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 伯宗弟伯興，官至前將軍、南平昌太守，直閣，領細仗主。

translations.literal: Bozong's younger brother Boxing reached office as General of the Vanguard, Prefect of Nanpingchang, Direct Attendant, and chief of the fine guard.
translations.idiomatic: Bozong's younger brother Boxing rose to General of the Vanguard, Prefect of Nanpingchang, Direct Attendant, and chief of the fine guard.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明元年，與袁粲同謀，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming of Emperor Shun, he plotted with Yuan Can and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Shengming era of Emperor Shun, he joined Yuan Can in a plot and was executed.

sentences.zh: 天與弟天生，少為隊將，十人同火。

translations.literal: Tianyu's younger brother Tiansheng, in youth was squad captain; ten men shared one fire.
translations.idiomatic: Tianyu's younger brother Tiansheng, in youth a squad captain, shared barracks with nine other men.

sentences.zh: 屋後有一大坑，廣二丈餘，十人共跳之皆渡，唯天生墜坑。

translations.literal: Behind the house was a great pit, more than two zhang wide; the ten together leaped it and all crossed—only Tiansheng fell into the pit.
translations.idiomatic: Behind their quarters was a pit more than two zhang wide; all ten leaped it and crossed—only Tiansheng fell in.

sentences.zh: 天生乃取實中苦竹，剡其端使利，交橫布坑內，更呼等類共跳，並畏懼不敢。

translations.literal: Tiansheng then took bitter bamboo from the fruit grove, shaved the ends sharp, crossed and laid them in the pit, and again called his companions to leap together—they all feared and dared not.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng cut bitter bamboo, sharpened the ends, and laid them crosswise in the pit, then called his comrades to jump again—they were all too afraid.

sentences.zh: 天生曰：「我向已不渡，今者必墜此坑中。

translations.literal: Tiansheng said: "I just now did not cross; now I must fall into this pit.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng said, "I failed to cross just now, so I am sure to fall into this pit again.

sentences.zh: 丈夫跳此不渡，亦何須活。

translations.literal: A man who leaps this and does not cross—what need is there to live?
translations.idiomatic: If a man cannot cross this, what reason has he to live?

sentences.zh: 」乃復跳之，往反十餘，曾無留礙，眾並嘆服。

translations.literal: Then he leaped again; back and forth more than ten times, never once hindered—all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Then he leaped again, back and forth more than ten times without a single stumble, and all marveled.

sentences.zh: 以兄死節，為世祖所留心，稍至西陽王子尚撫軍參軍，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Because his elder brother died in loyal integrity, he was noted by Shizu, and gradually reached Staff Officer to Prince Zishang of Xiyang, the General Who Rouses Dragons added.
translations.idiomatic: Because his elder brother died a loyal death, Emperor Xiaowu took notice of him, and he eventually rose to Staff Officer to Prince Zishang of Xiyang, with the additional title General Who Rouses Dragons.

sentences.zh: 隸沈慶之攻廣陵城，天生推車塞塹，率數百人先登西北角，徑至城上。

translations.literal: Under Shen Qingzhi attacking Guangling city, Tiansheng pushed carts to fill the moat, leading several hundred men to be first to scale the northwest corner, going straight to the top of the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Shen Qingzhi in the assault on Guangling, Tiansheng drove carts into the moat to fill it, then led several hundred men in the first scaling of the northwest corner and straight onto the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 賊為重柵斷攻道，苦戰移日，不拔，乃還。

translations.literal: The rebels built heavy palisades blocking the attack route; bitter fighting lasted a whole day; they could not take it, and so returned.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels threw up heavy barricades that blocked the assault, and after a full day of fierce fighting they still could not break through, so they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「天生始受戎任，甫造寇壘，而投輪越塹，率果先騰，驍壯之氣，嘉歎無已。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Tiansheng has only just received a military assignment and newly reached the bandit stronghold, yet cast aside wheels to cross the moat, leading resolutely to spring up first—fierce and brave in spirit; praise and sighing are unending.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Tiansheng has only just taken up arms and reached the rebel fort, yet he already cast aside his cart to cross the moat and led the charge up the wall. Such fierce courage fills us with unending admiration.

sentences.zh: 可且賜布千匹，以厲眾校。

translations.literal: He may for the time being be granted a thousand bolts of cloth, to encourage the various officers.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be granted a thousand bolts of cloth for the present, to hearten the other commanders.

sentences.zh: 」大明末，為弋陽太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Daming, he served as Prefect of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daming era, he became Prefect of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始初，與殷琰同逆，邊城令宿僧護起義討斬之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi under Emperor Taizong, he rebelled together with Yin Yan; Seng Hu, Magistrate of Biancheng, raised a loyal uprising and beheaded him in punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Taishi era under Emperor Ming, he joined Yin Yan in rebellion; Seng Hu, magistrate of Biancheng, raised loyal forces against them and executed him.

sentences.zh: 許昭先，義興人也。

translations.literal: Xu Zhaoxian was a man of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhaoxian was a native of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 叔父肇之，坐事繫獄，七年不判。

translations.literal: His uncle Zhaozhi, implicated in an offense, was imprisoned; seven years passed without judgment.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Zhaozhi was imprisoned on a criminal charge and languished in jail for seven years without trial.

sentences.zh: 子侄二十許人，昭先家最貧薄，專獨料訴，無日在家。

translations.literal: Among sons and nephews there were about twenty; Zhaoxian's family was poorest; he alone handled the litigation, not a day at home.
translations.idiomatic: There were some twenty sons and nephews in the family, but Zhaoxian's household was the poorest, so he alone pursued the case in court and was never home for a single day.

sentences.zh: 餉饋肇之，莫非珍新，家產既盡，賣宅以充之。

translations.literal: Provisions supplied to Zhaozhi were all fresh delicacies; family property was exhausted, and he sold the house to meet it.
translations.idiomatic: Everything he sent to sustain Zhaozhi in prison was fresh and choice food; when the family fortune was gone, he sold their house to pay for it.

sentences.zh: 肇之諸子倦怠，昭先無有懈息，如是七載。

translations.literal: Zhaozhi's sons grew weary; Zhaoxian had no slackening—for seven years thus.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozhi's own sons wearied of the effort, but Zhaoxian never slackened—for seven years straight.

sentences.zh: 尚書沈演之嘉其操行，肇之事由此得釋。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Director Shen Yanzhi praised his conduct and integrity; Zhaozhi's affair thereby obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yanzhi, Director of the Palace Secretariat, commended his character, and on that account Zhaozhi was released.

sentences.zh: 昭先舅夫妻並疫病死亡，家貧無以殯送，昭先賣衣物以營殯葬。

translations.literal: Zhaoxian's maternal uncle and wife both died of epidemic illness; the family was poor and had nothing for burial and sending-off; Zhaoxian sold clothing to arrange funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoxian's uncle and aunt both died in an epidemic; the family was too poor to bury them properly, so he sold his clothes to pay for their funeral.

sentences.zh: 舅子三人並幼，贍護皆得成長。

translations.literal: The uncle's three sons were all young; nourished and protected, all reached maturity.
translations.idiomatic: The uncle's three sons were still small children; Zhaoxian supported and cared for them until all three came of age.

sentences.zh: 昭先父母皆老病，家無僮役，竭力致養，甘旨必從，宗黨嘉其孝行。

translations.literal: Zhaoxian's parents were both aged and ill; the household had no servants; he exerted all strength to provide support; fine foods always attended; clan and neighbors praised his filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Both his parents were old and sick, and the household had no servants, yet he strained every effort to support them and always saw that delicacies were provided. Kinsmen and neighbors praised his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史劉真道板為征虜參軍，昭先以親老不就。

translations.literal: Yong Province Inspector Liu Zhendao appointed him Staff Officer under the General Who Punishes Barbarians; Zhaoxian because his parents were aged did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhendao, Inspector of Yong Province, appointed him staff officer to the General Who Punishes Barbarians, but Zhaoxian declined because his parents were elderly.

sentences.zh: 本邑補主簿，昭先以叔未仕，又固辭。

translations.literal: The local prefecture supplemented him as Chief Clerk; Zhaoxian because his uncle had not yet taken office, again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The local district then offered him the post of chief clerk, but he firmly refused again because his uncle had not yet received an appointment.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，西陽董陽五世同財，為鄉邑所美。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia, Dong Yang of Xiyang, five generations sharing property, was admired by the district and village.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanjia era, Dong Yang of Xiyang, whose family had held property in common for five generations, was admired throughout the countryside.

sentences.zh: 會稽姚吟，事親至孝，孝建初，揚州辟文學從事，不就。

translations.literal: Yao Yin of Kuaiji served his parents with utmost filial piety; at the beginning of Xiaojian, Yangzhou recruited him as Literary Attendant; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yin of Kuaiji was unfailingly filial toward his parents. At the opening of the Xiaojian era, Yang Province recruited him as literary attendant, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 余齊民，晉陵晉陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Qimin was a man of Jinling in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qimin was a native of Jinling county in Jinling commandery.

sentences.zh: 少有孝行，為邑書吏。

translations.literal: In youth he had filial conduct; he was a district clerk.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known for filial devotion and served as a district clerk.

sentences.zh: 父殖，大明二年，在家病亡，家人以父病報之。

translations.literal: His father Zhi, in the second year of Daming, died of illness at home; the family reported his father's illness to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daming his father Zhi died of illness at home; the family sent word that his father was sick.

sentences.zh: 信未至，齊民謂人曰：「比者肉痛心煩，有若割截，居常遑駭，必有異故。

translations.literal: Before the letter arrived, Qimin told people: "Lately my flesh ached and my heart was troubled, as if cut and severed; ordinarily I was constantly alarmed—there must be an unusual matter.
translations.idiomatic: Before the letter arrived, Qimin told those around him, "Lately my flesh has ached and my heart has burned, as though I were being cut apart. I have felt dread all the while—something terrible must have happened.

sentences.zh: 」信尋至，便歸，四百餘里，一日而至。

translations.literal: The letter soon arrived; he returned at once—more than four hundred li in one day.
translations.idiomatic: The letter came soon after, and he set out at once, covering more than four hundred li in a single day.

sentences.zh: 至門，方詳父死，號踴慟絕，良久乃蘇。

translations.literal: Reaching the gate, only then did he learn in detail that his father had died; he wailed, stamped, and grieved until he fainted; long after he revived.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached home he learned at last that his father was dead. He wailed and beat his breast until he collapsed in grief, and only after a long while did he come to.

sentences.zh: 問母：「父所遺言。

translations.literal: He asked his mother: "Father's remaining words.
translations.idiomatic: He asked his mother, "What were Father's last words?

sentences.zh: 」母曰：「汝父臨終，恨不見汝。

translations.literal: His mother said: "Your father at life's end regretted not seeing you.
translations.idiomatic: His mother said, "At the end your father grieved that he could not see you.

sentences.zh: 」曰：「相見何難。

translations.literal: He said: "Meeting him—what difficulty?
translations.idiomatic: He said, "What is so hard about seeing him?

sentences.zh: 」於是號叫殯所，須臾便絕。

translations.literal: Thereupon at the coffin he cried out; in a moment he expired.
translations.idiomatic: With that he cried out at the bier—and in an instant he was dead.

sentences.zh: 州郡上言，有司奏曰：「收賢旌善，萬代無殊，心至自天，古今豈異。

translations.literal: The province and commandery reported upward; the responsible office memorialized: "Gathering worthies and displaying goodness—ten thousand generations without difference; sincerity reaching from Heaven—past and present, how could they differ?
translations.idiomatic: The province and commandery reported the matter upward, and the responsible office memorialized: "To gather the worthy and honor goodness is a principle unchanged through the ages; when sincerity reaches from Heaven itself, how can past and present differ?

sentences.zh: 齊民至性由中，情非外感，淳情凝至，深心天徹，跪訊遺旨，一慟殞亡。

translations.literal: Qimin's utmost nature came from within; feeling was not from external influence; pure feeling condensed to the utmost; deep heart heaven-penetrating; kneeling he inquired of the last wishes; one burst of grief and he perished.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin's utmost nature sprang from within, not from outward prompting. Pure feeling condensed to its depth, and his heart pierced heaven itself. Kneeling, he asked after his father's last wishes—and in one convulsion of grief he died.

sentences.zh: 雖跡異參、柴，而誠均丘、趙。

translations.literal: Though his tracks differ from Zeng Shen and Gao Chai, his sincerity equals Zixia and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Though his outward deeds differ from those of Zeng Shen and Gao Chai, his sincerity matches that of Zixia and the Zhao exemplars.

sentences.zh: 方今聖務彪被，移革華夏，實乃風淳以禮，治本惟孝，靈祥歸應，其道先彰。

translations.literal: Now the sage's affairs splendidly spread, transforming and changing Huaxia—truly customs made pure by ritual, the root of governance is filial piety; auspicious responses return in accord—the Way first shines forth.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sage ruler's transforming work spreads far and wide, reshaping the Central Realm. Truly, custom is refined through ritual and the root of governance lies in filial piety; when auspicious signs answer in turn, this Way stands forth first of all.

sentences.zh: 齊民越自氓隸，行貫生品，旌閭表墓，允出在茲。

translations.literal: Qimin rose from common servile folk; conduct penetrating through the grades of the living; honor the hamlet and mark the tomb—truly it lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Qimin rose from humble commoners, yet his conduct touched every rank of the living. To honor his lane and mark his tomb is exactly what the occasion demands.

sentences.zh: 」改其里為孝義里，蠲租布，賜其母穀百斛。

translations.literal: His lane was changed to the Lane of Filial Righteousness; rent and cloth levies were exempted; his mother was gifted a hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: His neighborhood was renamed the Lane of Filial Righteousness, grain rents and cloth levies were remitted, and his mother was granted a hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 孫棘，彭城彭城人也。

translations.literal: Sun Ji was a man of Pengcheng in Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ji was a native of Pengcheng county in Pengcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 世祖大明五年，發三五丁，弟薩應充行，坐違期不至。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daming under Shizu, when the three-five draft was levied, younger brother Sa was to fulfill service but was punished for failing to arrive by the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, when the rotating draft was called up, his younger brother Sa was liable for service but was punished for arriving past the deadline.

sentences.zh: 依制，軍法，人身付獄。

translations.literal: According to regulations and military law, the person was handed over to prison.
translations.idiomatic: Under the regulations of military law, he was turned over to the prison.

sentences.zh: 未及結竟，棘詣郡辭：「不忍令當一門之苦，乞以身代薩。

translations.literal: Before the case was concluded, Ji went to the commandery to plead: "I cannot bear to let the whole household suffer; I beg to substitute myself for Sa.
translations.idiomatic: Before the case could be settled, Ji went to the commandery and pleaded, "I cannot bear to see the whole household suffer. I beg to take Sa's place.

sentences.zh: 」薩又辭列：「門戶不建，罪應至此，狂愚犯法，實是薩身，自應依法受戮。

translations.literal: Sa also pleaded in turn: "The household is not established; the crime deservedly reached here; foolishly breaking the law—the person is truly Sa himself; he should by law receive execution.
translations.idiomatic: Sa in turn submitted a plea: "Our household has no foundation yet, and the crime has rightly come to this. The fool who broke the law is Sa himself, and by law he alone should die.

sentences.zh: 兄弟少孤，薩三歲失父，一生恃賴，唯在長兄；

translations.literal: The brothers were orphaned young; Sa at three lost his father; his whole life relied—only on the elder brother;
translations.idiomatic: The brothers lost their father while still young. Sa was only three when their father died, and all his life he has depended on his elder brother alone.

sentences.zh: 兄雖可垂愍，有何心處世。

translations.literal: The elder brother though may be shown pity—what heart to live in the world.
translations.idiomatic: You may pity my brother, but if he lives on, what heart will he have left for this world?

sentences.zh: 」太守張岱疑其不實，以棘、薩各置一處，語棘云：「已為諮詳，聽其相代。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhang Dai suspected it was untrue; he placed Ji and Sa each in a separate place and told Ji: "Already submitted a detailed report; allowing mutual substitution.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Dai doubted their sincerity, so he kept Ji and Sa apart and told Ji, "I have already reported the matter in full and will allow you to take each other's place.

sentences.zh: 」棘顏色甚悅，答云：「得爾，旦則為不死。

translations.literal: Ji's expression was very pleased; he replied: "Getting this, then I am not dead.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's face brightened with joy, and he answered, "If that is granted, then I am as good as alive.

sentences.zh: 」又語薩，亦欣然曰：「死自分甘，但令兄免，薩有何恨！

translations.literal: He also told Sa, who likewise gladly said: "Death I myself accept willingly; only let the elder brother be spared—what regret has Sa!
translations.idiomatic: When he told Sa as well, Sa also said gladly, "I accept death willingly—so long as my brother is spared, what regret can Sa have!

sentences.zh: 」棘妻許又寄語屬棘：「君當門戶，豈可委罪小郎。

translations.literal: Ji's wife Xu also sent a message entrusting Ji: "You uphold the household—how can you shift the blame to the younger brother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's wife Xu also sent word to him: "You are the pillar of this household. How can you leave the blame to your young brother-in-law?

sentences.zh: 且大家臨亡，以小郎屬君，竟未妻娶，家道不立，君已有二兒，死復何恨。

translations.literal: Moreover when father-in-law was dying he entrusted the younger brother-in-law to you; he has not yet married; the household way is not established; you already have two sons—what regret in death?
translations.idiomatic: When your father-in-law lay dying he entrusted the boy to you. Sa is still unmarried and the family line is not yet secure, while you already have two sons. What regret would there be in your death?

sentences.zh: 」岱依事表上，世祖詔曰：「棘、薩氓隸，節行可甄，特原罪。

translations.literal: Dai memorialized according to the facts; Shizu edict said: "Ji and Sa, common servile folk—integrity and conduct can be distinguished; specially pardon the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dai reported the matter upward, and Emperor Xiaowu decreed, "Ji and Sa are humble commoners, yet their integrity and conduct deserve recognition. Their offense is specially pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」州加辟命，並賜許帛二十匹。

translations.literal: The province additionally appointed them and gifted Xu twenty bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The province further appointed them to office and granted Xu twenty bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 先是，新蔡徐元妻許，年二十一，喪夫，子甄年三歲，父攬愍其年少，以更適同縣張買。

translations.literal: Previously, Xu, wife of Xu Yuan of Xincai, age twenty-one, lost her husband; son Zhen was age three; father Lan pitying her youth, remarried her to Zhang Mai of the same county.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xu, wife of Xu Yuan of Xincai, was twenty-one when her husband died, leaving a son Zhen aged three. Her father Lan, pitying her youth, arranged to remarry her to Zhang Mai of the same county.

sentences.zh: 許自誓不行，父逼載送買。

translations.literal: Xu vowed herself not to go; her father forced her, loaded her, and sent her to Mai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu vowed she would not go, but her father forced her into a cart and sent her to Zhang Mai.

sentences.zh: 許自經氣絕，家人奔赴，良久乃蘇。

translations.literal: Xu hanged herself and her breath stopped; the family rushed to her; long after she revived.
translations.idiomatic: Xu hanged herself and lost consciousness. Her family rushed to her side, and only after a long while did she revive.

sentences.zh: 買知不可奪，夜送還攬。

translations.literal: Mai knew it could not be taken away; by night he sent her back to Lan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Mai saw that her resolve could not be broken, and that night sent her back to her father.

sentences.zh: 許歸徐氏，養元父季。

translations.literal: Xu returned to the Xu family; she nourished Yuan's father Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Xu returned to the Xu household and supported her late husband's father Ji.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，年八十餘，卒。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era, age over eighty, she died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanjia era she died at over eighty years of age.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始二年，長城奚慶思殺同縣錢仲期。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi under Emperor Taizong, Xi Qingsi of Changcheng killed Qian Zhongqi of the same county.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Taishi era under Emperor Ming, Xi Qingsi of Changcheng murdered Qian Zhongqi, a man of the same county.

sentences.zh: 仲期子延慶屬役在都，聞父死，馳還，於庚浦埭逢慶思，手刃殺之，自繫烏程縣獄。

translations.literal: Zhongqi's son Yanqing was on assigned corvée service in the capital; hearing his father had died, he rushed back; at Gengpu ferry dam he encountered Qingsi, personally blade-killed him, and voluntarily imprisoned himself in Wucheng county jail.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqi's son Yanqing was on corvée duty in the capital. When he heard of his father's death he raced home, met Qingsi at the Gengpu ferry, and killed him with his own hand, then surrendered himself to the jail of Wucheng county.

sentences.zh: 吳興太守郗顒表不加罪，許之。

translations.literal: Wu Xing Prefect Xi Yong memorialized not to add crime; it was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Yong, Prefect of Wu Xing, memorialized that no further punishment should be imposed, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 何子平，廬江灊人也。

translations.literal: He Ziping was a man of Qian in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Ziping was a native of Qian in Lujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖楷，晉侍中。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Kai was Jin Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Kai served as Palace Attendant under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 祖友，會稽王道子驃騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Grandfather You was Staff Officer on the General of Agile Cavalry Secretariat of Prince Daozi of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather You was staff officer on the secretariat of Prince Daozi of Kuaiji, General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父子先，建安太守。

translations.literal: Father Zixian was Prefect of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zixian was Prefect of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 子平世居會稽，少有志行，見稱於鄉曲。

translations.literal: Ziping generation after generation resided in Kuaiji; in youth he had ambition and conduct; he was praised in the local community.
translations.idiomatic: Ziping's family had long lived in Kuaiji. From youth he showed purpose and integrity, and was praised in his neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 事母至孝。

translations.literal: He served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He was unfailingly filial toward his mother.

sentences.zh: 揚州辟從事史，月俸得白米，輒貨市粟麥。

translations.literal: Yangzhou recruited him as Attendant Secretary; monthly salary obtained white rice—he always sold it for millet and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Province recruited him as attendant secretary, he always sold the white rice from his monthly salary and bought millet and wheat instead.

sentences.zh: 人或問曰：「所利無幾，何足為煩？

translations.literal: Someone asked: "The profit is slight—why bother?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked him, "The gain is trifling—why go to the trouble?

sentences.zh: 」子平曰：「尊老在東，不辦常得生米，何心獨饗白粲。

translations.literal: Ziping said: "My honored elder is in the east and cannot always obtain raw rice—what heart to enjoy white grain alone.
translations.idiomatic: Ziping replied, "My mother lives in the east and cannot always get unhulled grain. How could I bear to eat polished white rice by myself?

sentences.zh: 」每有贈鮮肴者，若不可寄致其家，則不肯受。

translations.literal: Whenever there were gifts of fresh delicacies, if they could not be sent to his home, he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he was given fresh delicacies, he refused the gift if it could not be sent on to his mother.

sentences.zh: 母本側庶，籍注失實，年未及養，而籍年已滿，便去職歸家。

translations.literal: His mother was originally a secondary wife; the household register notation failed truth; her actual age had not yet reached the nurture requirement, but the register age was already full—he left office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had been a concubine, and the household register recorded her age incorrectly. She was not yet old enough in fact to qualify for his retirement to care for her, but on the register she was—so he resigned his post and went home.

sentences.zh: 時鎮軍將軍顧覬之為州上綱，謂曰：「尊上年實未八十，親故所知。

translations.literal: At that time General Who Pacifies the Army Gu Yunzhi was chief provincial officer; he said to him: "Your honored mother's actual age is not yet eighty—relatives and friends know.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gu Yunzhi, General Who Pacifies the Army and chief provincial officer, said to him, "Your mother's true age is not yet eighty. Relatives and friends all know it.

sentences.zh: 州中差有微祿，當啟相留。

translations.literal: In the province there is a modest salary; I will open a petition to retain you.
translations.idiomatic: There is a modest salary here in the province, and I shall petition to keep you in office.

sentences.zh: 」子平曰：「公家正取信黃籍，籍年既至，便應扶侍私庭，何容以實年未滿，苟冒榮利。

translations.literal: Ziping said: "The public office rightly takes trust in the Yellow Register; register age having arrived, one ought to support and attend in the private home—how tolerate because actual age is not full, carelessly claim glory and profit.
translations.idiomatic: Ziping said, "The state relies on the Yellow Register. Once the register says she is old enough, I ought to go home and serve her. How could I use her real age as an excuse to cling to rank and profit?

sentences.zh: 且歸養之願，又切微情。

translations.literal: Moreover the wish to return and nurture is also urgent in private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, my wish to return and care for her comes from the deepest private feeling.

sentences.zh: 」覬之又勸令以母老求縣，子平曰：「實未及養，何假以希祿。

translations.literal: Yunzhi again urged him to use his mother's age to seek a county post; Ziping said: "Truly not yet reached nurture age—why borrow it to hope for salary.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yunzhi urged him again to use his mother's age as grounds for seeking a county post. Ziping said, "She is truly not yet old enough. Why should I use that as a pretext to seek a salary?

sentences.zh: 」覬之益重之。

translations.literal: Yunzhi valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yunzhi respected him all the more.

sentences.zh: 既歸家，竭身運力，以給供養。

translations.literal: Having returned home, he exhausted his body exerting strength to provide support.
translations.idiomatic: Once home, he spent himself in labor to provide for his mother.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三十年，元兇弑逆，安東將軍隨王誕入討，以為行參軍。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Yuanjia, the usurper committed regicide; General Who Pacifies the East Prince Dan of Sui entered to punish; he was made Traveling Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Yuanjia the regicide Liu Shao murdered the emperor. Prince Dan of Sui, General Who Pacifies the East, marched to punish him and appointed Ziping traveling staff officer.

sentences.zh: 子平以凶逆滅理，普天同奮，故廢己受職，事寧，自解。

translations.literal: Ziping because the villain extinguished principle and all under Heaven rose together, therefore abandoned himself to accept office; when the affair was settled, he resigned of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ziping felt that the traitor had overturned all moral order and that the whole realm had risen as one, so he set aside his own wishes and accepted the post. When the campaign ended, he resigned on his own.

sentences.zh: 又除奉朝請，不就。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was next appointed Court Gentleman for Attendance, but declined.

sentences.zh: 末除吳郡海虞令，縣祿唯以養母一身，而妻子不犯一毫。

translations.literal: Lastly he was appointed Magistrate of Haichang in Wu Commandery; county salary was used only to nourish his mother's person—and wife and children did not touch a single hair.
translations.idiomatic: He was finally appointed magistrate of Haichang in Wu commandery. He used his county salary only to support his mother, and neither his wife nor his children touched a penny of it.

sentences.zh: 人或疑其儉薄，子平曰：「希祿本在養親，不在為己。

translations.literal: Someone suspected him of being stingy; Ziping said: "Hoping for salary originally lies in nurturing kin—not in serving oneself.
translations.idiomatic: When some thought him miserly, Ziping said, "I sought office to support my mother, not myself.

sentences.zh: 」問者慚而退。

translations.literal: The questioner, ashamed, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The questioner withdrew in shame.

sentences.zh: 母喪去官，哀毀逾禮，每至哭踴，頓絕方蘇。

translations.literal: When his mother died he left office; grief destroyed him beyond ritual; each time of weeping and stamping, he instantly fainted and then revived.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office and mourned beyond all measure. Each time he wept and beat his breast he collapsed, only to revive again.

sentences.zh: 值大明末，東士饑荒，繼以師旋，八年不得營葬，晝夜號絕擗踴，不闋俄頃，叫慕之音，常如袒括之日。

translations.literal: It happened at the end of Daming; eastern lands had famine; followed by army returns; eight years he could not arrange burial; day and night he cried until fainting, beat breast and stamped—not pausing a moment; calling and yearning sound always like the day of baring shoulder for coffining.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daming era the eastern provinces suffered famine, and troop movements followed on its heels, so for eight years he could not bury her. Day and night he wailed until he fainted, beating his breast without a moment's pause, his cries of longing as raw as on the day he had bared his shoulder beside her coffin.

sentences.zh: 冬不衣絮，暑避清涼，日以數合米為粥，不進鹽菜。

translations.literal: In winter he wore no padded clothes; in summer he avoided cool places; daily several he of rice made into porridge; he did not eat salt or vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he wore no padded garments; in summer he shunned cool shade. Each day he ate only a few he of rice boiled into gruel, with neither salt nor vegetables.

sentences.zh: 所居屋敗，不蔽雨日，兄子伯興採伐茅竹，欲為葺治，子平不肯，曰：「我情事未申，天地一罪人耳，屋何宜覆。

translations.literal: The house where he dwelt was ruined and did not shield from rain and sun; elder brother's son Boxing gathered and cut thatch and bamboo, wishing to repair it; Ziping would not agree and said: "My emotional duty is not yet fulfilled—I am heaven and earth's one guilty man—why should the house be roofed?
translations.idiomatic: The house he lived in was falling in and gave no shelter from rain or sun. His nephew Boxing gathered thatch and bamboo to repair it, but Ziping refused, saying, "My filial duty is still unfulfilled. I am a guilty man before heaven and earth—why should my roof be mended?

sentences.zh: 」蔡興宗為會稽太守，甚加旌賞。

translations.literal: Cai Xingzong as Prefect of Kuaiji greatly added commendation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xingzong, Prefect of Kuaiji, greatly honored and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年，為營塚槨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi, he had a tomb mound and inner coffin built for her.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taishi he had a tomb and inner coffin built for her.

sentences.zh: 子平居喪毀甚，困瘠逾久，及至免喪，支體殆不相屬。

translations.literal: Ziping in mourning grief destroyed greatly; emaciated and wasted ever longer; when mourning ended, his limbs nearly did not connect to each other.
translations.idiomatic: Ziping's mourning had wasted him severely. He grew ever more gaunt, and by the time mourning ended his limbs scarcely seemed to belong to the same body.

sentences.zh: 幼持操檢，敦厲名行，雖處暗室，如接大賓。

translations.literal: From youth he held to conduct and restraint; earnestly admonished name and conduct; though dwelling in a dark room, as if receiving a great guest.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he held himself to strict conduct and cultivated his reputation. Even alone in a private room he behaved as though receiving an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 學義堅明，處之以默，安貧守善，不求榮進，好退之士，彌以貴之。

translations.literal: Study of principles firm and clear; dwelling in silence; content with poverty, guarding goodness; not seeking glory and advance—men who value withdrawal prized him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: His learning in principle was firm and clear, and he met the world in quiet reserve. Content with poverty and steadfast in goodness, he sought no advancement, and men who valued withdrawal esteemed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 順帝昇明元年，卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengming of Emperor Shun, he died; age at the time sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Shengming era of Emperor Shun he died, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：漢世士務治身，故忠孝成俗，至乎乘軒服冕，非此莫由。

translations.literal: The historian says: In the Han era scholars devoted themselves to cultivating the person; therefore loyalty and filial piety became custom; reaching the point of riding carriages and wearing caps—not by this there was no path.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: In Han times scholars devoted themselves to self-cultivation, and loyalty and filial piety became the common way of life. To ride in carriages and wear official regalia, there was no other path.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋以來，風衰義缺，刻身厲行，事薄膏腴。

translations.literal: From Jin and Song onward, wind decayed and righteousness lacked; carving the body and sharpening conduct—the affair was thin compared to fat lands.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin and Song, mores have decayed and righteousness grown thin. Those who mortify the flesh and discipline their conduct are scarce among the privileged.

sentences.zh: 若夫孝立閨庭，忠被史策，多發溝畎之中，非出衣簪之下。

translations.literal: As for filial piety established in inner chambers and loyalty recorded in historical annals—many arose from irrigation ditches, not from beneath robe and hairpin.
translations.idiomatic: When filial piety flourishes within the household and loyalty earns a place in the histories, it often springs from humble ditches and fields—not from the ranks of robed officials.

sentences.zh: 以此而言聲教，不亦卿大夫之恥乎！

translations.literal: By this speaking of teaching and transformation—is it not the shame of ministers and grandees!
translations.idiomatic: To speak of moral transformation on such grounds—is it not the shame of the ministerial class!
